articles.title: Paralympic champions Pramod Bhagat, Bhavina Patel to lead India as flag bearers at Asian Para Games

articles.body: NEW DELHI: After a successful Asian Games campaign in Aichi-Nagoya, where India finished fourth in the medal tally with 85 medals, including 21 gold, the country's para-athletes will look to carry the momentum into the Asian Para Games.Paralympic champions Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel have been chosen as India's flag bearers for the Opening Ceremony of the Asian Para Games, scheduled to be held from October 18 to 24 in Nagoya, Japan.Bhagat, one of India's most decorated para badminton players, has won six Asian Para Games medals between 2014 and 2023, including two gold and four bronze. Patel, meanwhile, is among India's leading para table tennis players and has won two Asian Para Games medals — a silver and a bronze — between 2018 and 2023.‘A very proud moment’Patel said being selected to carry the Tricolour was a matter of immense pride and hoped the honour would inspire the Indian contingent.“It is a very proud moment for me to be chosen as India's flag bearer,” Patel said in a release.“When you carry the Tricolour, you realise that you are representing something much bigger than yourself. I am excited to walk into the Opening Ceremony with Pramod and lead our contingent. I hope all our athletes compete with confidence, enjoy the moment and give their very best for India.”The Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) will formally send off the Indian contingent at a special ceremony on October 8. Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya will attend as chief guest, with Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Nikhil Khadse as the Guest of Honour.‘Fitting representatives of the Indian contingent’PCI president Devendra Jhajharia said Bhagat and Patel's achievements and resilience made them ideal choices to lead India at the continental para-sport showpiece.“It is a matter of immense pride for us to have Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel lead the Indian contingent at the Opening Ceremony,” Jhajharia said.“Both are exceptional champions who have contributed immensely to the growth of Indian para sport. Their journey, achievements and resilience make them fitting representatives of the Indian contingent, and I am confident they will inspire our athletes as they embark on this important campaign.”The Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games will bring together para-athletes from across Asia, with India aiming to build on its growing success at major international competitions.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: UCLA Has 'Serious Concern' QB Nico Iamaleava Will Miss The Rest Of The Season
articles.summary: Nico Iamaleava is expected to remain out indefinitely with the knee injury. While a final timeline remains pending a full medical evaluation, there is a real chance he could miss the rest of the season.
articles.body: The UCLA Bruins are the biggest story in college football right now, but their momentum could be on the verge of slipping. Following the upset win in Eugene over No. 13-ranked Oregon, the Bruins improved to 5-0 under first-year head coach Bob Chesney. However, winning came at a cost as quarterback Nico Iamaleava exited the game early with a knee injury. According to ESPN, Iamaleava is expected to remain out indefinitely with the knee injury. While a final timeline remains pending a full medical evaluation, there is a real chance he could miss the rest of the season – Chesney has said as much, stating that there's "serious concern" that Iamaleava could miss the rest of the year. "I'm going to wait for our doctors to make the final call," Chesney said Monday at his weekly news conference. "There is some serious concern at the moment. But at the same point in time, there's nothing that has been fully ruled at this moment. There's still other opinions and other people we want to talk to, to make sure everyone sees it the same way." Iamaleava's play on the field has been sub-par this season, but he’s been one of the stabilizing factors in the Bruins' impressive start. Through five games, he has completed 62.1% of his passes for 982 yards, four touchdowns, and four interceptions. With Iamaleava sidelined, Chesney and his staff must turn to either Ty Dieffenbach or Madden Iamaleava, Nico’s younger brother. Nico threw for 162 yards against Oregon before exiting with the injury and being replaced by Dieffenbach. In relief for Iamaleava, Dieffenbach completed 3-of-6 passes for 43 yards and a touchdown against the Ducks. Madden Iamaleava had been considered the backup earlier this season, but Chesney could now open up a competition or even utilize a two-quarterback system. During his time at James Madison, Chesney frequently deployed multi-quarterback systems. He often paired primary starter Alonza Barnett III with other options like transfer Matthew Sluka and JC Evans for specialized running and passing packages. With the Bruins remaining undefeated and ranked No. 12 nationally, the injury couldn’t come at a worse time. Even though Iamaleava hasn’t fully lived up to his five-star recruiting hype, he will still have one year of eligibility remaining for the 2027 season. articles.title: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel Expected To Miss Multiple Weeks With Hamstring Injury
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. is expected to miss “at least a couple of weeks" with the hamstring injury he suffered Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks.
articles.body: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. is expected to miss "at least a couple of weeks" with the hamstring injury he suffered Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters. Samuel was ruled out with a hamstring injury in the third quarter against the Seattle Seahawks. The injury occurred when Samuel was running toward the sideline when he fell to the ground, fumbling in the process, before being seen by training staff. Samuel was eventually able to make his way off the field, holding his right leg before being ruled out. It was the second loss of the day for the 49ers in Seattle after linebacker Dre Greenlaw was ejected in the second quarter after he headbutted Seahawks linebacker Ernest Jones IV during a sideline scuffle following a late hit on Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold. Samuel is in his first season back in San Francisco after spending last season with the Washington Commanders, where he had 72 catches for 727 yards and five touchdowns. He rejoined the 49ers on a one-year deal this past offseason. With Samuel sidelined, Brandin Cooks, who had a receiving touchdown in the fourth quarter, could be the next in line to absorb his workload. articles.title: Jacob Misiorowski’s Lesson From Adam Wainwright Has Gone ‘A Long Ways’
articles.summary: Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski detailed how Cardinals' legend Adam Wainwright has impacted his pitching style through Milwaukee's postseason run.
articles.body: The Milwaukee Brewers got off to a 2-0 lead in the National League Championship Series over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday, and ace Jacob Misiorowski played a major role in the Game 1 win. Misiorowski, who is in his second postseason run with the Brewers, allowed one run on five hits with five strikeouts and three walks over 4 1/3 innings against the reigning World Series champions in Sunday's win. And he credited much of that outing to former St. Louis Cardinals ace and current MLB on FOX commentator Adam Wainwright. When FOX Sports’ David Ortiz asked Misiorowski during the MLB on FOX pregame show before Monday's Game 2 win, Misiorowski immediately credited Wainwright for impacting his mindset. "Honestly, big shoutout to Wainwright," Misiorowski said. "I got to talk with him and got to pick his brain a little bit on how to watch video of myself, and brought that into this one, and really stuck with my game plan instead of trying to adapt to the game too much. It worked out." For Misiorowski, who grew up outside of Kansas City, Missouri, Wainwright has always been the inspiration behind his baseball talent and his pitching style. Now, looking up to Wainwright, who played 18 seasons for the Cardinals and was part of their 2006 World Series-winning team, his simple pieces of advice have played a big part in Misiorowski's success as a pitcher. The 24-year-old right-hander has been the anchor of Milwaukee’s rotation, and that was on full display Sunday, when he took the ball opposite Dodgers ace and two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal. When talking about Wainwright’s impact with FOX Sports’ Kevin Burkhardt, Misiorowski explained how it changed his approach. "The biggest one was the mindset of watching film. I would really get down on myself and couldn’t really watch film by myself. I would get frustrated and have to turn it off," Misiorowski said. "Wainwright was telling me to think about it differently." So how did Wainwright change the way "Miz" watches film? By keeping it simple. "Before, I was critical of every little movement," Misiorowski said. "Now, Wainwright’s like, ‘Hey, focus on little things. Instead of fixing it, plan on how to make it better,’ and that’s helped a lot." That one simple lesson has helped turn the Brewers’ starter into one of the most dominant pitchers in baseball in just two seasons. This postseason, Misiorowski has allowed three runs on nine hits over 8 1/3 innings. With a fastball that routinely tops 100 mph and has even reached the 105-mph mark, he has delivered in big moments as Milwaukee tries to get past the Dodgers, who swept the Brewers in last year’s NLCS, and hand Los Angeles its first postseason elimination since 2023. articles.title: David Ortiz Predicts Dodgers' Loss, Noting Los Angeles Is In 'Deep Trouble'
articles.summary: FOX Sports' David Ortiz weighed in on the Dodgers' postseason struggles following the Dodgers' 7-4 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 2 of the NLCS.
articles.body: The Dodgers lost their second straight NLCS game after falling 7-4 to the Brewers, recording just three hits against Milwaukee's pitching. FOX Sports' David Ortiz was the only one at the MLB on FOX pregame show desk to predict the Brewers win in Game 2. Why?"I have never seen the Dodgers offense be this poor," Ortiz said.He was able to take his victory lap postgame. "Papi, you called it!" FOX Sports' Alex Rodriguez said to his co-analyst. "You’re the only one who called it." L.A.'s bullpen gave up seven runs and 12 hits to Milwaukee as the Dodgers' offense struggled to put points on the board. Even Dodgers' Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who is historically a solid postseason pitcher, struggled to keep the Brewers scoreless. But the Dodgers still have a chance to turn things around.This time, with the Dodgers down 2-0, the stakes are even higher entering Game 3 in Los Angeles. "The Dodgers are in some deep trouble," Ortiz said. "They haven’t been able to put it together offensively. They are 2-for-26 with men on base. I told you." The Dodgers' underwhelming performance is tied to several parts of the roster, but one is clear. Two-way star Shohei Ohtani hasn't delivered any solid showings since returning from injury. In 16 at-bats leading up to Game 2, Ohtani has hit .188 with three hits. Tonight, Ohtani went 0-for-4 with two strikeouts. For the four-time MVP, the numbers don't match the powerhouse that Ohtani has been in past postseason runs with Los Angeles. While Ohtani remains a major factor in whether the Dodgers can bounce back, FOX Sports' Derek Jeter didn't deny that Los Angeles is in trouble against a red-hot Brewers offense. "It's tough, man. It's tough to turn your entire team around offensively when you're going up against a team like the Milwaukee Brewers… I agree, the Dodgers are in trouble," Jeter said. "Unless they can figure out how to string together some hits. Because on top of them (the Dodgers) being in a little bit of trouble, now the Milwaukee Brewers offense is getting hot … This is going to be the biggest hurdle they're going to have to overcome if they want to go back and win a third championship in a row." The Dodgers' resume proves it's an organization built to win. It's home to a four-time MVP in Ohtani, and it's chasing its third consecutive World Series Championship. After its second consecutive postseason loss, Ortiz noted Los Angeles's lack of offense on the diamond."It’s difficult to watch these guys not score runs offensively," Ortiz said. "We know that the Dodgers are capable of scoring runs offensively, but nobody is hitting. The unexpected has happened, and they are facing good pitching."Like I always say: good pitching can always stop good offense." articles.summary: Sydney Sweeney ironiza sobre las críticas del deporte a su anterior campaña publicitaria y saca otro provocador anuncio
articles.body: Sydney Sweeney vuelve a protagonizar un nuevo anuncio para la empresa de pronósticos deportivos Novig, e ironiza sobre las críticas generadas por su campaña publicitaria anterior. En la anterior campaña la famosa actriz desató una gran polémica con su anuncio de "Just Sports" (Sólo Deportes) posando desnuda y utilizando equipamientos deportivos para cubrirse. El anuncio generó rápidamente gran revuelo, y reacciones negativas dentro del mundo del deporte ("es una falta de respeto sexualizar cuerpos para un anuncio"), ya que los críticos argumentaban que sexualizaba el deporte y eclipsaba a las deportistas. "Nuestro cuerpo no es el espectáculo, pero lo que somos capaces de hacer sí", compartió la exgimnasta Lourdes Mohedano. En su nuevo anuncio Sydney Sweeney empieza diciendo que "hay hombres adultos haciendo hojas de cálculo para apostar sobre el color de la ropa interior que llevo. Quiero decir, me siento halagada". La protagonistas de la serie 'Euphoria' subraya que "hay operaciones con información privilegiada sobre la muerte de dictadores y ejércitos de bots que manipulan todo". "Hay alguien sentado en un baño apostando su fondo de jubilación por una guerra y, después, están las personas que operan con deportes", comparte. Sydney Sweeney sentencia que "Novig es… sólo deportes".

articles.title: 3 Takeaways as depleted Spurs fall to Jazz
articles.summary: With Victor Wembanyama and three other starters looking on from the bench, the Spurs dropped a 119-109 decision at the Delta Center.
articles.body:
SALT LAKE CITY - The Spurs starters got in a good sweat.

After going through a more intense than usual shootaround in the morning, all but one of the regulars had the night off. Playing with a skeleton crew, the Spurs remained winless in the preseason after losing 119-109 to Utah on Monday night at the Delta Center.

The Spurs (0-3) rested Victor Wembanyama, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell . De'Aaron Fox, who has yet to make his preseason debut because of a hip injury, and Carter Bryant , who suffered an ankle injury in the 102-98 loss at Phoenix on Saturday , also sat out the game.

All five Jazz starters scored in double figures, with rookie Darryn Peterson, the No. 2 overall pick, finishing with 14 to go along with five assists. Jaren Jackson Jr. and Keyonte George each had 13 points to help Utah improve to 2-1.

Spurs second-round rookie Ja'Kobi Gillespie scored 15 of his game-high 25 points in the fourth quarter on 6-of-8 shooting from the field and 3 of 4 from 3-point range. He was 9 of 14 and 4 of 8 overall in 25 minutes.

Harrison Barnes had 19 points on the strength of 10-of-12 shooting from the free-throw line. Keldon Johnson, who turned 27 on Sunday, had 15 points, while Julian Champagnie and Jordan McLaughlin had 14 apiece.

Spurs coach Mitch Johnson pulled his starting five of Barnes, Johnson, Champagnie, McLaughlin and Luke Kornet mid-way through the third quarter. Champagnie is the only starter from the first two exhibition games that saw action in Salt Lake City.

"I was really happy with the starting five and the whole group," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "I thought there's been some carryover from new things we've installed or implemented, things that maybe we've tweaked or tried to grow. And then some things in terms of just playing to our identity and our standard and style of play that probably has not been up to the standard that we felt like it should.

"We put our energy and intentions into a lot of good spots tonight."

Here are three takeaways from a game featuring teams that will meet again on Oct. 28 in the first of three regular season games, all in the first three weeks of the season:

Rookie center Tarris Reed Jr. wears No. 10, and at times he resembled one of the greatest rebounders in NBA history, a Hall of Famer who also wore that number as a Spur.

Like Dennis Rodman, the 6-foot-10, 270-pound Reed was relentless on the boards.

Reed had 10 rebounds - six on the offensive glass - in his first six minutes. He finished with 17, including eight on the offensive end, in 24 minutes.

"Rebounding is one of those things where you don't really get free ones, so if you go get 17 of them, that means you're working," Mitch Johnson said. "And I think he will continue to see more pictures or things and patterns over time and recognize things and the game will slow down. But right now I love the physicality and the motor he's playing with. He just has a nose for the basketball, and, typically, that's a very valuable skill set in this league."

Reed also had four points, four steals, one assist and one block.

But it was his rebounding that stood out.

"I feel like it was a good job, a good step forward on the glass today, knowing that was the emphasis for this team," Reed said. "So keep being dominant, keep being physical, and whatever I need to do to help this team out, I'll do it."

In sitting Wembanyama, Castle and other mainstays, the Spurs simply followed a load-management plan mapped out before the preseason by the medical staff.

Given the cramped preseason schedule, a break in Utah at the midway point was a smart move.

"Just management in terms of we got five games every other day and had a good practice this morning," Mitch Johnson said. "And so just trying to continue to get into in-season game shape as best we can, which is a little bit of a balancing act, and give some opportunities for other guys that have earned it."

Wembanyama, Castle, Harper and Vassell are all expected to return Wednesday at home against Phoenix.

"Optimistic, but I'm not sure they're going to play, but they're trending in the right way," Mitch Johnson said.

The Spurs have already ruled out Tobias Harris for the entire preseason due to a left calf strain. Rookie Jayden Quaintance is out indefinitely while rehabbing from offseason knee surgery after the Spurs drafted him 20th overall.

3. McLaughlin great for end-of-bench role

It wasn't one of the marquee moves of the offseason, but Spurs general manager Brian Wright re-signing Jordan McLaughlin made Mitch Johnson and others in the organization smile.

With Castle and Harper out, the eighth-year pro started at point guard and produced 14 points on 6-of-10 shooting and six assists.

"He executes exactly what's asked of him and plays with composure," Mitch Johnson said.

The players were also glad the Spurs brought back McLaughlin to add depth and leadership at the end of the bench.

"Anytime we need him to come in, he's ready to play," Keldon Johnson said. "He's always positive and he's just an amazing teammate."

McLaughlin said he briefly looked at Atlanta, Boston and Utah before deciding to sign a one-year, $3.3 million deal with the Spurs.

"You hear nothing but good things before coming into the organization, but when you're in it and you actually see it, they take care of their players," he said. "The players take care of the players. We've got a good group, good group of guys, very talented group of guys, and we all enjoy each other's company."

articles.title: Kyren Williams grinds out 76 yards and a touchdown
articles.summary: Kyren Williams turned 22 touches into a combined 76 yards and a score during the team's Week 5 loss to Buffalo.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams RB Kyren Williams ran the ball 16 times for 49 yards and a touchdown against the Buffalo Bills in Week 5. Williams added six catches (on eight targets) for 27 yards in the loss.

Why It Matters: Williams didn't find a lot of room to run in Week 5, averaging just 3.1 yards per catch and 4.5 yards per reception. He found the end zone in the closing moments, however, salvaging his value for the week. Even though the production wasn't there against Buffalo, Williams still registered 22 combined touches. While the presence of Blake Corum prevents Williams from being a surefire RB1, the Notre Dame product is a high-end RB2 that will produce like an RB1 some weeks.

articles.title: Golden Knights achieve a pair of firsts, but fall short of comeback to Wild
articles.summary: SAINT PAUL—For a minute there, it looked like the cardio machine the Vegas Golden Knights have transformed themselves into over the past season or so was abo...
articles.body:
SAINT PAUL—For a minute there, it looked like the cardio machine the Vegas Golden Knights have transformed themselves into over the past season or so was about to switch back on.

However, it was ultimately not to be, as the Golden Knights started out a quick back-to-back road trip on the wrong foot with a 4-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild on Monday.

While the Golden Knights started the game strong, a failed power play would begin a tilting of the ice in the other direction.

Shortly after the man advantage expired, the Golden Knights were dealing with a disadvantageous scenario with Rasmus Andersson breaking his stick. Wild forward Matt Boldy would catch Noah Hanifin looking for the puck, giving him a couple of free opportunities that eventually got past Carter Hart.

From there, the deluge began. The Wild would not make a mistake on their power play, as Maxim Shabanov's shot squeaked by Hart to add to the Minnesota lead. It was quickly followed by Danila Yurov getting a clean look on a cross-ice pass, and the Golden Knights found themselves down 3-0 in the span of just over five minutes.

Despite the Wild dominating the second period in terms of opportunities, the Golden Knights would manage to find some life.

Getting some redemption for what was a rough first period, Andersson would tee up a slapshot that beat Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt cleanly, allowing the Golden Knights to cut into the lead.

More significantly, though, was that forward Raphael Lavoie would get his long-awaited first NHL point on the secondary assist.

Needing a third period push, defenseman Jeremy Lauzon tried to ignite his team with a fight against Wild forward Rieger Lorenz.

While the decision to fight the rookie was not taken kindly to by other Wild players, it did manage the desired effect. Mitch Marner would find Brett Howden with a clean breakout pass to set up an odd-man rush, and Howden's pass would find William Karlsson that allowed the center to pick up his first goal of the season and put the Knights back within one.

However, the luck would run out before an equalizer was found, as broken sticks from Brayden McNabb and Karlsson would lead to Joel Eriksson Ek icing the game in favor of the Wild with an empty-net goal.

Hoping to get off to a faster start, the Golden Knights face a quick turnaround as the annual Frozen Frenzy sees them taking on the Nashville Predators on Tuesday.

articles.title: Commanders’ collapse vs. Giants is so bad that 1 fan broke sobriety
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders ended up with their first tie of the season after their Week 5 matchup against the New York Giants finished 27-27 in overtime. How...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders ended up with their first tie of the season after their Week 5 matchup against the New York Giants finished 27-27 in overtime . However, the result felt more like a loss for Washington, as the team squandered multiple opportunities to close out the game. The frustrating finish was so painful for one fan that it reportedly even threatened his month-long sobriety .

JP Finlay of NBC4 Sports shared the heartbreaking reaction of a Washington fan who called into a show following the Commanders' disappointing result.

"We just had a caller who said he was 1 month sober and yesterday broke him. 'Had to go back to the cabinet after that,"' Finlay wrote.

The Commanders appeared to have the game under control after building a 27-13 lead with just over 11 minutes remaining in regulation.

Washington's defense had also delivered a strong performance during the first half, limiting New York to just 26 rushing yards. That total tied for the fifth-fewest rushing yards the Giants had recorded against Washington in franchise history.

However, the Giants found their rhythm in the second half, with quarterback Jameis Winston leading the charge. The veteran signal-caller completed 33 of 54 pass attempts for 326 yards and three touchdowns.

Meanwhile, one of the biggest positives for Washington was Jayden Daniels' return to the field after missing the previous two games with a dislocated left elbow. The young quarterback delivered a productive performance, completing 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards.

Daniels also added 103 rushing yards and two touchdowns on the ground. The Commanders QB made history with his rushing production, becoming the first Washington quarterback to record nine rushing touchdowns within the first three seasons of his career.

However, the tie left Washington at 1-3-1, while the Giants improved to 3-1-1. The result was particularly frustrating for the Commanders, given how close they came to winning .

Washington will now turn its attention to a challenging road game against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night in Week 6.

articles.summary: Harry Smith is named alongside captain George Williams in the England half-back roles for their 2026 Rugby League World Cup opening match against Tonga - wit...
articles.body:
Harry Smith has been named alongside captain George Williams in England's half-back roles for their Rugby League World Cup opening match against Tonga - with Mikey Lewis left out.

Lewis, who pipped 2025 Super League Man Of Steel Jake Connor to a place in England's squad, has not even made the bench for Saturday's fixture.

Hull KR's Lewis, who endured an inconsistent year, did enough to convince England head coach Brian McDermott that he should join captain Williams, the Warrington stand-off, and Wigan's Smith as half-back options.

But he will be one of three players, along with Ben Currie and Ben Talty, listed as non-playing reserves.

England face Tonga in Perth on Saturday (10:05 BST), before taking on France in the same city on 24 October and then Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on 30 October.

England men: AJ Brimson, Dom Young, Hugo Savala, Herbie Farnworth, Zach Eckersley, George Williams, Harry Smith, Max King, Brad O'Neill, Morgan Knowles, Junior Nsemba, Kai Pearce-Paul, Victor Radley.

Interchange: Jez Litten, Luke Thompson, Ethan Havard, Sam Walters, Jack Welsby, Matty Ashton.

McDermott, who succeeded Shaun Wane in April, has also made a major selection call at full-back.

AJ Brimson has been chosen ahead of Jack Welsby in the key role for England's first game in Group B-C - a combined pool of six teams, from which the top two will go through to the semi-finals early next month.

McDermott indicated that he was keen to use heritage players - those who qualify for England through family background - to ensure the strongest possible squad.

And Brisbane-born Brimson - who made his England debut in last year's Ashes series against Australia - is one of four such players in the squad, alongside England debutant Max King.

Bulldogs prop King, born in Huddersfield while his Australian father David was a player there, features alongside fellow debutant Hugo Savala, part of Sydney Roosters' NRL Grand Final-winning squad. Victor Radley is also in the XIII.

All of the men's and women's teams for the first round of matches between Thursday and Sunday were announced on Tuesday at 06:00 BST.

England women's coach Stu Barrow named his squad for their opener against Wales on Saturday in Perth (07:35 BST).

Jasmin Strange and Connie Boyd will make their international debuts, while uncapped Hope Millard is among the interchanges.

Opponents Wales will give a debut to second-row forward Paige Travis - who played for England at the last World Cup four years ago.

Tayla Preston - who captains Canterbury Bulldogs in the NRL Women's Premiership - will start at scrum-half, with former rugby union international Ffion Lewis alongside her at stand-off, while Hannah Bluck will represent Wales at a fourth different sport.

Bluck has won senior Wales honours in rugby union as well as gaining junior rank recognition in football and basketball.

Reece Walsh has been selected ahead of James Tedesco at full-back for Australia - co-hosts and men's World Cup favourites - as they face New Zealand in the tournament's opening match on Thursday (10:05 BST).

Walsh was the star player in Australia's 3-0 Ashes series whitewash of England last year, but has endured a tougher 2026.

Injury has prevented Walsh from playing since August 15, while Tedesco won the Clive Churchill medal for best player in the 2026 Australian National Rugby League Grand Final.

But head coach Kevin Walters has stuck with Walsh in a backline that includes Test debutant Jack Bostock on one wing and Tom Trbojevic on the other.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Sports Ministry has dropped under-fire para-shooting coach Jai Prakash Nautiyal from India's contingent for the Asian Para Games 2026,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Sports Ministry has dropped under-fire para-shooting coach Jai Prakash Nautiyal from India's contingent for the Asian Para Games 2026, approving a 166-athlete squad for the continental event in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, amid a controversy-marred selection process that triggered protests by shooters and cyclists.The Games are scheduled to begin on October 18, with India set to compete across 10 disciplines. Long-serving national coach Jeevan L Rai has replaced Nautiyal in the squad following allegations of irregularities in the selection process.As per a PTI report, Nautiyal had faced allegations of not following established selection criteria and demanding kickbacks in exchange for selecting shooters. Several athletes protested outside the Sports Authority of India (SAI) headquarters, demanding his removal and an investigation into the charges.The aggrieved shooters also met Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya to present their grievances after attempting to disrupt the contingent's send-off ceremony last week.With 166 athletes approved, India will have a total contingent of 275, including 94 team officials and support staff and 15 contingent staff members.Controversial shooting selection; cyclists' protest fails to change squadThe 13-member shooting squad, which has been at the centre of the controversy, features Paralympic gold medallist Avani Lekhara and Mona Agarwal, among others. Agarwal recently secured a silver medal at the World Championships in Korea, earning India a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics.The Ministry has also resisted pressure for last-minute additions to the cycling squad despite protests by omitted athletes. Only Paralympian Arshad Shaik was approved from among those in contention, having comfortably met the selection criteria.Six other cyclists had been selected by the Cycling Federation of India and the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI), but were subsequently left out for failing to satisfy the prescribed criteria.The decision comes amid questions over the selection process, with athletes seeking greater transparency in the composition of the Indian contingent.Sheetal Devi, Bhavina Patel among India's medal hopesPara-athletics forms the biggest part of India's contingent, with 62 athletes, including 46 men, and a support staff of 36. World Championships medallist Simran, a visually impaired sprinter, is also part of the squad. After her previous guide, Umar Saifi, was caught in a doping case, she will compete with a new guide, Shivam.India's other medal prospects include Paralympic silver medallist Bhavina Patel in table tennis and a strong badminton contingent of 28 players, comprising 17 men and 11 women.Former world No. 1 and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat and former Paralympic silver medallist Suhas Yathiraj headline the badminton squad, which has been allocated 11 support staff members.In archery, 19-year-old Sheetal Devi, a double gold medallist at the previous Para Asian Games, will be among India's leading contenders. The world champion will be joined by 18-year-old Payal Nag, who grabbed attention by defeating Sheetal at the World Archery Para Series in Bangkok earlier this year.With a sizeable contingent and several established champions in its ranks, India will look to make a strong impression in Japan, even as the selection controversy casts a shadow over the team's preparations.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 30 años del coche que hasta Cristiano Ronaldo acabó comprándose
articles.standfirst: ¿Cuántos Audi A3 te has cruzado hoy? Seguro que más de uno porque ya se han producido más de seis millones de unidades. Así han sido las cuatro generaciones del compacto que se presentó en París hace justo tres décadas
articles.summary: ¿Cuántos A3 te has cruzado hoy? Seguro que más de uno porque ya se han producido más de seis millones de unidades. Así han sido las cuatro generaciones del compacto que se presentó en París hace justo tres décadas
articles.body: Treinta años. Es lo que ha pasado desde que el Audi A3 se estrenó en el Salón de París de 1996, y la edad a la que muchos consideran que ya han dejado de ser jóvenes. Pero el tiempo pasa de forma diferente para personas y coches y el modelo de los cuatro aros se ha reinterpretado a sí mismo a lo largo de estas tres décadas, en las que ha pasado por cuatro generaciones, se ha comercializado en más de 100 países y han salido de la cadena de montaje más de seis millones de veces. Con el Audi A3 aprendimos que un coche compacto también podía ser 'premium' (más bien de gama alta, porque hace 30 años no empleábamos esa palabra). Esta es la historia de un modelo que en la actualidad tiene 17 variantes entre carrocerías y motores, con Sportback, Sedan y allstreet, gasolina, diésel, híbrido enchufable y los deportivos S3 y RS 3. Y sí, hasta Cristiano Ronaldo se compró uno, como te vamos a explicar. El A3 original llegó como modelo de tres puertas, con la cintura baja y mucha superficie acristalada que, según Audi, le daban "aspecto de coupé". Dentro apostaba por el acabado y una buena ergonomía, y su equipamiento dependía de que eligiéramos los acabados Attraction, Ambition y Ambiente, para los que hubo cuatro motores de gasolina y cuatro diésel. El primer gran hito llegó en septiembre de 1998 con la variante quattro, que estrenaba la tracción integral en este segmento empleando un embrague multidisco de control electrónico en la entrada del diferencial trasero. En 1999 llegó la carrocería de cinco puertas, pero lo 'bueno' fue una versión el S3 muy radical que equipaba un motor turbo de 1,8 litros con 210 CV, dos intercoolers, tracción integral, cambio manual de seis velocidades y asientos Recaro. Uno de los que cayó rendido a este S3 fue Cristiano Ronaldo, que por entonces no era más que un jovencísimo futbolista al que nadie reconocía por CR7. Y después, ya en 2001, el S3 ascendió a 225 CV. Más longitud, más distancia entre ejes y más anchura. Los pasajeros ganaron espacio y confort, y el A3 ganó tamaño. También llegaron nuevos motores de cuatro y seis cilindros, un cambio de doble embrague de siete velocidades para las versiones más potentes, una nueva suspensión trasera independiente de cuatro brazos y la dirección electromecánica. En 2004 apareció el Sportback, con 65 milímetros (6,5 cm) más de batalla que el cinco puertas anterior. Fue el primer A3 con la parrilla Singleframe, inspirada en la que ya llevaba el A8 y que acabaría siendo 'la cara' de la marca. Según Audi, sigue siendo hoy la carrocería más vendida del A3. En 2008 llegaron el S3 Sportback, con 265 CV, y el primer A3 Cabrio, con capota de lona. Y en 2011, el RS 3, con cinco cilindros, 340 CV y tracción total. Es decir, 130 CV más que el primer S3. Por algo se lo consideró como uno de los hot hatch modernos. Fue el primer Audi sobre la plataforma modular transversal MQB, que permitió una construcción más ligera, más soluciones digitales y más variantes. El aluminio rebajó el peso de la carrocería. Dentro contaba ya con mando giratorio, control por voz y conexión con el móvil. Además, estrenó asistentes de segmentos superiores, como el control de crucero adaptativo y los de cambio y mantenimiento de carril. Los motores siguieron la moda del downsizing: menos cilindrada e incorporación de turbocompresores. Se estrenó, además, el cylinder on demand, que apaga dos de los cuatro cilindros con poca carga. En 2013 llegó el A3 Sedan, que atrajo a clientes nuevos (más fuera de Europa que dentro). Un año más tarde apareció el A3 Sportback e-tron, el primer híbrido enchufable compacto de la marca. Pero lo impactante llegó en 2016 con el RS 3 Sedan, el primer Audi compacto de tres volúmenes con el emblema RS, animado por un 2.5 TFSI de 400 CV. La generación actual llegó con un diseño más deportivo, luces diurnas configurables, mucho manejo táctil por medio de la pantalla central y, en algunos motores, hibridación ligera de 48 voltios. En 2021 llegó el nuevo RS 3, movido por un cinco cilindros con más par y beneficiado por el torque splitter en el eje trasero, formado por dos embragues multidisco que reparten el par entre las ruedas traseras y sustituyen al sistema Haldex. Acelera de 0 a 100 km/h en 3,8 segundos y alcanza 290 km/h, así que se puede considerar como un auténtico deportivo disfrazado de coche compacto. Audi también nos sorprendió en 2024 al sacar el A3 allstreet, un crossover con tres centímetros más de distancia al suelo que el Sportback y una posición de asiento más elevada. Y ese mismo año el S3 se actualizó con 333 CV (245 kW), sistema de tracción quattro con torque splitter, eje delantero más deportivo y dirección optimizada. Treinta años dan para mucho. El A3 se ha fabricado siempre en Ingolstadt, pero desde 1999, también en Brasil (en Sao José dos Pinhais) y a principios de los 2000 se sumó la planta húngara de Gyor. Todo para dar abasto a la demanda de un coche que sigue teniendo mucha vida por delante.

articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck and Goalie Trade Options for the Rangers After Igor Shesterkin Injury
articles.summary: After a strong offseason that saw them address a lot of pressing roster issues, including goal-scoring depth and rounding out their top four on defense, there was some reason for optimism for the New York Rangers entering the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
After a strong offseason that saw them address a lot of pressing roster issues, including goal-scoring depth and rounding out their top four on defense, there was some reason for optimism for the New York Rangers entering the 2026-27 season.

The optimism only grew with a strong start that was largely driven by starting goalie Igor Shesterkin.

Then everything was thrown into chaos when the Rangers announced Saturday that Shesterkin would miss the rest of the season after suffering an injury Friday against Washington.

That not only leaves a major hole in their lineup, but it also takes away one of the few players the team has been able to consistently rely on over the past six years.

By every objective measure we have to evaluate goalies, Shesterkin is one of the best in hockey. He has always lifted the Rangers and covered for a lot of their defensive shortcomings.

Taking him out of the lineup for the remainder of the season is a devastating blow to their playoff chances. Dylan Garand is a solid prospect and has played well this season, but it's a long campaign, and the Rangers are one of the most goalie-dependent teams in the league. This could be a problem.

It also opens the door for a potential trade, especially with veteran goalie Joonas Korpisalo still sidelined for the immediate future.

So let's take a look at the Rangers' options: absurd and unrealistic possibilities, players they should avoid and more logical rentals.

The Keep Dreaming Option: Connor Hellebuyck, Winnipeg Jets

It is the biggest elephant in the room, so you kind of have to address it.

But it's also an elephant that you can probably keep ignoring, even after acknowledging its existence.

On the surface, you can kind of see why people would try to connect Hellebuyck to the Rangers, as Sportsnet Insider Elliotte Friedman did , although he also stated the unlikelihood of it happening.

He is the type of elite goalie who could immediately step in for Shesterkin and allow the Rangers to keep going forward as planned.

He has been one of the few goalies over the past few years who have matched—and at times exceeded—Shesterkin's level of play. He is a Hall of Fame-bound player with three Vezina Trophies and an Olympic gold medal. His goals saved above expected numbers have consistently been among the best in the NHL, finishing in the top 10 in five of the past six seasons and leading the league three times.

Hellebuyck also wants out of Winnipeg and is still waiting for a trade that has yet to come, and at some point, you would think everybody involved wants some kind of resolution to this situation.

If the Rangers were a top Stanley Cup contender, maybe you would consider it. But they are not, and that means it probably would not make sense to pay the price for Hellebuyck.

There is also the matter of contracts and the fact that both Hellebuyck and Shesterkin are signed to long-term deals. Neither player is going to want to split time in net, and it would not make sense for the Rangers to pay two elite goalies a combined $20 million per year for the foreseeable future—even with a consistently rising salary cap.

Maybe you could argue that the Rangers could turn around after the season and flip Hellebuyck to somebody else. But that is probably easier said than done, and may not result in them getting back as much as they would have to give up.

It's a fun idea. It would also be the type of chaotic, outrageously aggressive move NHL teams tend to avoid. It just doesn't seem realistic and certainly not likely.

The Option to Avoid: Jordan Binnington, St. Louis Blues

Joel Hofer is the best goalie in St. Louis, and he is starting to wrestle playing time away from Binnington.

Given that development, as well as the fact that Binnington is in the final year of his contract, he could be somebody the Blues look to trade if they can find a taker for him.

Given the way hockey people still seem to believe in the 33-year-old as a big-game goalie and a winner, they might even succeed in doing that.

But the Rangers should not be the team, even on a short-term basis or as a stopgap for this season.

More often than not, Binnington has been one of the worst goalies in the league, finishing minus-9 or worse in goals saved above expected in three of the past five seasons. He ranked 90th or worse in those three seasons, and he has not looked good in his first two appearances this season.

Putting him behind a Rangers team that still gives up a lot of chances and is very goalie-dependent would not be a winning move.

Potentially Realistic Option: Philipp Grubauer, Seattle Kraken

Grubauer had a lot of success early in his career with the Washington Capitals and Colorado Avalanche, and parlayed that into a big contract with the Seattle Kraken in their inaugural expansion season.

The hope was that he could be a stabilizing presence in goal and give an emerging franchise a chance to compete.

Over the first few years of his deal, it just never really worked out as hoped.

But since the start of the 2025-26 season, Grubauer has bounced back and been a pretty solid goalie. Joey Daccord is the starter in Seattle and the younger of the two netminders, which could make the pending UFA Grubauer a potential trade chip.

It's hard to imagine that he would cost a lot in terms of draft picks or assets, and he might be able to at least give the Rangers some league-average play and a chance to keep competing in the Eastern Conference playoff race.

Can Rangers Survive Without Shesterkin? 😓

Potentially Realistic Option: One of the Los Angeles Kings Goalies

The Los Angeles Kings enter play on Tuesday as one of the three winless teams in the NHL, along with the Philadelphia Flyers and Calgary Flames.

It is too soon for them to give up on the season or become obvious sellers, but they do have two veteran goalies on expiring contracts: Darcy Kuemper and Anton Forsberg.

They are both off to slow starts this season, but they could be the type of potential stopgap that might make some sense if the Rangers do not feel comfortable going forward with Garand and Spencer Martin until Joonas Korpisalo's return later this season.

There is also the question of whether or not either one of them would actually be better than Korpisalo, but you have to take into account the fact that when he does return, he may not be 100 percent or at his most effective.

It would at least be an option to explore.

Potential Wild-Card Option: Karel Vejmelka, Utah Mammoth

This would require some moving parts and would also indirectly (or perhaps directly) involve Hellebuyck.

Utah has been mentioned as a potential landing spot for Hellebuyck, and he would help put them on the map as a possible Western Conference Stanley Cup contender.

If they get him, they may not have as much long-term use for Vejmelka.

Could they then flip him to the Rangers as part of a separate deal? Could New York get involved as a third team in a hypothetical Winnipeg-Utah deal?

Vejmelka could help this season, but his $4.75 million cap hit through 2029-30 would represent a substantial commitment for a goalie expected to back up Shesterkin beyond this year.

Is it a long shot? Yes, but there are worse options and definitely less interesting ones.

articles.title: Carmelo Hayes' Star-Making Moment Out of Nowhere, WWE's Massive Stakes Fresh Feud, More Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The October 12 edition of Raw on Netflix aired from the Brookshire Grocery Arena in Bossier, Louisiana, delivering major fallout from Money in the Bank.
articles.body:
The October 12 edition of Raw on Netflix aired from the Brookshire Grocery Arena in Bossier City, Louisiana, delivering major fallout from Money in the Bank.

The 946 collided with The Bloodline, receiving some extra help courtesy of Carmelo Hayes. Chelsea Green stopped by to face down her Crown Jewel opponent, Liv Morgan, only to lose to Roxanne Perez.

Bron Breakker speared Je'Von Evans again while ruining Penta's Money in the Bank celebration. Chad Gable delivered another great TV match against Rey Fénix.

For all the fallout from an important episode of Raw, keep reading.

Carmelo Hayes Will Become a World Title Challenger with The 946

Carmelo Hayes has a new direction after aligning with the hottest heel faction in WWE, The 946.

From no direction on SmackDown to feuding with The Bloodline, Melo is in position to rise all the way to genuine world title contention.

While Royce Keys is still the apparent leader of the group, Melo is a better worker and talker than Keys and will have plenty of chances to prove it.

Of everyone in the faction, Melo has the most obvious upside, and it will be obvious quickly in the coming months.

Few have impressed more in the ring than Him when he gets opportunities, and this is by far his biggest opportunity on the main roster.

The driving star of NXT could easily be a threat to Roman Reigns or Oba Femi with The 946 behind him on the rise.

Bron Breakker vs. Je'Von Evans Will Be One of WWE's Most Defining Feuds

Bron Breakker at 28 years old and Je'Von Evans at 22 are among the highest-profile young stars in WWE right now.

While The Young OG was already in conflict with The Vision, the feud between Breakker and Evans kicked off in the men's Money in the Bank ladder match on Saturday.

The Badass' targeting of Evans—particularly sending him crashing through the top of an ambulance—established their feud as a major storyline on Raw.

This feud has potential to define WWE for the next 10 to 15 years as both grow into their roles.

This could genuinely be the great rivalry of this era, even if it will take time to fully get to that point.

Breakker looks poised to become world champion in 2027, and Evans would be a great underdog challenger for the newly crowned titleholder.

In the coming years, both men should hold multiple titles and can consistently cause each other problems on their road to success.

Chelsea Green Must Beat Liv Morgan at Crown Jewel

Crown Jewel is set for November 7 when the world champions will collide for the title of Crown Jewel champion.

Of the four world champs heading to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, only one has already held a Crown Jewel Championship: Liv Morgan.

There is no reason for Morgan to win again so soon, and Chelsea Green winning over Liv would be a massive boost for the WWE women's champion.

Since winning, Green has been presented as a scrappy underdog, struggling to find her way to success. She even lost to Roxanne Perez in non-title action on Raw.

Winning the Women's Crown Jewel Championship would be an accolade no one could ignore and solidify Green's place among the best women's wrestlers in WWE right now.

Morgan would lose nothing by failing to become the first-ever two-time Crown Jewel champion. Green would gain lasting credibility.

WWE Must Book Stephanie Vaquer vs. Becky Lynch

While Liv Morgan heads toward a match with Chelsea Green to determine the top name in the women's division, it is two women suddenly out of the title picture that are the most interesting.

Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch have begun to tease that their conflict will lead to a big first-time-ever contest.

While La Primera is recovering from injury after Money in the Bank, she still appeared on Raw, which would indicate it is a short-term injury.

WWE should use that time to keep building anticipation for the inevitable clash that showed real promise in the teases between them in the Money in the Bank triple threat.

What matters most is that WWE makes the most of the match. It should not be wasted on TV. It should be a major collision at a premium live event.

Time for Ethan Page to Dethrone Chad Gable

Chad Gable has delivered three great title defenses on Raw as intercontinental champion, but the story focus of only defending against luchadors is growing stale.

Victories over Rey Mysterio, Dragon Lee and Rey Fénix after dethroning Penta have exhausted the obvious luchador challengers unless WWE wants to bring in AAA talent.

The better option would be to refocus on who is available on Raw, particularly "All Ego" Ethan Page, who has been chomping at the bit for a shot for months.

Page already impressed when he fought Penta at Saturday Night's Main Event, and he is ready to turn another opportunity into a big win.

All Ego may be the most talented underserved star on Raw. It would make sense to reheat him by letting Page dethrone Gable.

It could be the beginning of a strong rivalry between the two talented wrestlers while also freshening up the title scene immediately.

articles.title: 10 Fun New Food Concessions at NHL Arenas This Season
articles.summary: The beginning of the NHL season is a time of joy and optimism.
articles.body:
The beginning of the NHL season is a time of joy and optimism.

Hockey is back on our screens and in our arenas. No one is out of the playoff race yet. And increasingly, arena concession programs are delighting fans with new food items that are as inventive as they are unhinged.

Pierogies are tucked into a deli sandwich. Soft-serve ice cream is slathered in butter (yes, butter). And in what may be the most viral new food offering around NHL arenas this season, Nerds Gummy Clusters are stuffed into a grilled cheese.

Keep reading to find out which teams are unveiling these fun and outrageous bites. Who knows; maybe you'll be lucky enough to find them at your own team's barn.

Canadian Tire Centre (Ottawa Senators): Sen-Sational Poutine Burger

It's nice to know that poutine isn't just a stereotypical food we assume Canadians love but that they never actually eat. Poutine is, in fact, a staple in Canada, even outside Quebec, to the point that it's the backbone of this new burger on offer at Ottawa Senators games this season.

The burger features braised Canadian bison, classic poutine gravy and cheese curds, and smashed crispy potato tots. Perhaps the most eye-catching part of this package, however, is the Senators' helmet-shaped container it's served in, which feels like it's taken a page out of the collectible movie popcorn bucket trend.

The Sen-Sational Poutine Burger is available in Section 210 for $18.89 CAD.

Enterprise Center (St. Louis Blues): Louie's Snack Den Loaded Popcorn Bowls

These build-your-own popcorn bowls at Louie's Snack Den (Portal 31) have all the hallmarks of a viral food item in 2026.

Not only are they eminently photographable for social media, but the do-it-yourself nature of selecting the toppings for your own popcorn bowl is the same impetus that has made dirty soda such a popular phenomenon. People love to have a hand in creating their own treat.

Fans can choose from two bowl sizes. From there, they select a drizzle (white chocolate, milk chocolate, or caramel) and can add up to three included toppings (M&M's, Oreo cookie pieces, toffee pieces, gummy bears, mini marshmallows, pretzels). If you're going for a true garbage popcorn, additional toppings are $1 each.

Grand Casino Arena (Minnesota Wild): Butter-Dipped Ice Cream Cone

At first glance, this photo may make you wonder why this food item deserves inclusion on a list of items that includes blue Takis on cased meats and a fully playable popcorn bucket.

But don't let the seemingly innocuous vanilla ice cream cone pictured here fool you. This daring dairy dessert features vanilla soft serve dipped in melted butter, which quickly hardens, like the far more typical chocolate magic shell topping. It's a viral culinary trend started by regional grocery chain Stew Leonard's that has spread across the U.S.

At Grand Casino Arena, the concoction is topped with flaky sea salt and served up in a waffle cone.

Prudential Center (New Jersey Devils): Playable Popcorn Bucket

Playable popcorn bucket: surprising, innovative, exciting.

That's what the Devils are going for this season with their viral, first-of-its-kind playable popcorn bucket. The collectible features pinball-style paddles on a miniature hockey rink that lets fans use pieces of popcorn as pucks to try to score goals into the nets.

The clever collectible is available at multiple locations throughout the concourse.

PPG Paints Arena (Pittsburgh Penguins): Ultimate Penguinator

It doesn't get much more Pittsburgh than this over-the-top sandwich.

Each bite of the Ultimate Penguinator reveals a surprising new taste of the city. The base is a normal, if excessive, deli sandwich: turkey, roast beef, ham, provolone and cheddar. Then things go off the rails.

Layered on top are mozzarella sticks, waffle fries, and pierogies(!). This monster is piled onto herb Italian bread and topped with lettuce, tomato, and roasted garlic ranch.

The Ultimate Penguinator is also served in a Pittsburgh bridge-themed box, in case the theme wasn't clear. It can be found at the Fifth Avenue Food Hall in Section 116.

Rogers Place (Edmonton Oilers): Loaded Helmet Nachos

Is any food item loaded into a helmet all that out there in 2026? No, but that doesn't make this offering any less fun or desirable, especially for a kid: It's junk food and a souvenir in one.

For these loaded nachos, Rogers Place didn't reinvent the wheel. The slop bowl (complimentary) features corn tortilla chips, cheese sauce, shredded cheddar, sour cream, salsa, jalapeños, and green onions.

If you have strong opinions on the shape of your tortilla chip, these are circles. (If you have no idea what this means, just keep reading; it's not for you.)

SAP Center (San Jose Sharks): K-Chomp Corn Dog

A popular undercurrent of viral arena food is to continually reinvent and reimagine the humble arena dog.

The San Jose Sharks' offering is a dog that leans into Korean flavors. A spicy Louisiana sausage is topped with pepper jack cheese and Korean BBQ sauce.

However, the pièce maîtresse of this dog, and what will endear it to Sharks fans, is the blue Takis sprinkled on top.

The K-Chomp Corn Dog is available at Club 117 inside SAP Center for $13.25.

TD Garden (Boston Bruins): Souvenir Draft Beer Hockey Glove

During last year's NHL playoffs, the Carolina Hurricanes' viral Beer Skate became the hottest item fans could get their hands on. When it debuted at the Lenovo Center, fans snapped up 4,867 in a single game.

The Buffalo Sabres' Beer Sabre and the Utah Mammoth Tusk Mug have similarly attracted fans' eyeballs (and dollars).

Later in October, the Boston Bruins are throwing their hat into the collectible beer mug arena, serving up beverages in a vessel shaped like a hockey glove.

The Bruins have not yet shared details on where in TD Garden the glove will be available or how much it will cost, but the team encourages fans to keep an eye on the Bruins and TD Garden mobile app for announcements.

UBS Arena (New York Islanders): Nerds Gummy Cluster Brie Grilled Cheese

A true Mad Lib of a concessions item, stuffing Nerds Gummy Clusters into a brie grilled cheese seems about as random as it gets.

How do these wacky food items come to be? In this case, reports The Athletic's Kaitlyn Pohly , UBS Arena executive chef Ted Donnelly and his team scroll through food videos on TikTok and Instagram, searching for inspiration. Ideas with promise get written on a whiteboard in an office in the arena.

Pohly, who had an opportunity to try the screwball sandwich, notes that the combination isn't as random as one might expect, bringing "the sweetness of a jam you might pair with brie on a cheese board."

United Center (Chicago Blackhawks): Beef and Chicken Tortas

Chicago is home to the fifth-largest Mexican population in the United States, so it's no surprise to see tortas, a Mexican street-food staple, join the lineup at the United Center's Corona Beach concessions stand this season.

The new tortas are available with chicken or beef and are served on a soft telera roll with shredded lettuce, tomatoes, refried beans, queso fresco and sour cream, alongside housemade tortilla chips and salsa.

While the torta isn't an uncommon item in Chicago's neighborhoods, it doesn't often find its way onto arena menus, making for a nice change of pace from chicken tenders and burgers.

articles.title: Paul Rowley: Castleford Tigers appoint former St Helens boss as head coach on three-year deal after departure of Ryan Carr
articles.summary: Castleford Tigers have appointed Paul Rowley as their head coach on a three-year contract with the club only being kept off the bottom of Super League by Bradford Bulls last season
articles.body:
Rowley left St Helens in July with the club on their way to missing out on the Super League play-offs for the first time, having previously been in charge of Salford prior to the club's financial collapse in 2025.

He takes over at the Tigers following the departure of Australian Ryan Carr for personal reasons two months ago.

"I'm looking forward to leading Cas Tigers as their new head coach," said Rowley, who becomes Castleford's seventh head coach since Daryl Powell departed in 2021.

"From meeting [director of rugby] Chris [Chester] and the board, it immediately felt like a place I wanted to be a part of. I'm keen to get started and enjoy a new journey with this proud club."

Chester said: "We're absolutely delighted to welcome Paul Rowley to Castleford Tigers as our new head coach.

"Paul is a highly-respected coach within rugby league, and we believe he is the right person to lead this club into an exciting new chapter."

Chester also admitted there is the prospect of further recruitment in the coming weeks and months, adding: "I'm looking forward to working closely with Paul as we continue to strengthen the squad, develop our young talent and create a culture that delivers sustained success.

"We're delighted to have him on board and look forward to seeing what we can achieve together."

Castleford finished second bottom in Super League with only eight wins from their 27 games.

articles.title: Schubert logra lo nunca visto: repite una de las cinco vías del mundo con el grado máximo de dificultad
articles.standfirst: Completa la ruta 'DNA' que Seb Boulin abrió en 2022 y catalogó como 9c. Es la primera vez que se logra encadenar por segunda vez una ascensión con este nivel de complejidad
articles.summary: Completa la vía 'DNA' que Seb Boulin abrió en 2022 y catalogó con el grado de máxima dificultad. Es la primera repetición de una de las cinco rutas de este nivel que existen en el mundo
articles.body: Desde que Adam Ondra lograra en 2017 la primera vía acreditada como 9c ('Silence' en Flatanger, Noruega), el grado máximo de dificultad en la escalada libre, otras cuatro ascensiones se han catalogado en este nivel, pero ninguna había sido repetida para acreditar este nivel de complejidad. Jakob Schubert ha sido el primero en completar por segunda vez una de estas rutas: 'DNA' en las Gargantas del Verdon (La Ramirole, Francia) que fue abierta por Seb Boulin en 2022. Schubert era uno de los cinco escaladores con una 9c en su haber. En 2023 había completó 'B.I.G.', también en Flatanger. Los otros dos integrantes de este selecto club, más allá de los mencionados Ondra y Boulin, son Sean Bailey con 'Duality of man' en Dry Canyon (Arizona) y el español Jorge Díaz-Rullo con 'Café Colombia', en la zona de Margalef (Tarragona). Schubert, medallista de bronce en los Juegos de París y en los de Tokio, retransmitió su ascensión a 'DNA' en directo a través de YouTube. Se fijó el video de la ascensión de Boulin para planificar su subida. En su día, el francés tardó tres años en equipar 'DNA'. Empleó 250 intentos en 150 días hasta llegar a completarla el 29 de abril de 2022. Una vez conseguido dudó si era una 9b+ o 9c. "Tuve que modificar algunos detalles porque soy mucho más bajo que él, pero pude copiar gran parte de la información, lo que me ahorró mucho tiempo", reconoce a 'Climbing'. El escalador austriaco ya había acometido esta ruta por primera vez en 2024. Desde entonces ha dedicado más de 30 días, en varios periodos de tiempo, hasta esta tanda en la que, al noveno intento, completó los 1,75 m de esta vía. "Al principio había vuelto a dudar de si tenía lo necesario mentalmente para encadenar esta ruta porque es una batalla mental tan intensa. Es con diferencia la vía más dura que he intentado nunca", apuntó el escalador austríaco al que le quedaba la duda de si era la primera repetición de una 9c porque al mismo tiempo Will Bosi lo intenta en 'Silence' (todavía sin éxito). Adam Ondra no tardó en felicitarle en los comentarios de la retransmisión en YouTube que va ya por cerca de 300.000 visualizaciones. "¡Qué pasada, Jakob! Una escalada impresionante; manejaste la presión de la retransmisión en directo y esa ventana meteorológica de tres días como un auténtico maestro, ¡y lograste encadenar!". Junto al checo Schubert tiene previsto intentar 'Exodia', la escalada de bloques con el nivel más difícil del mundo tras ser propuesta como 9A+ por el italiano Elias Iagnemma hace un año. Schubert, once veces medallista en los Mundiales de escalada (con cuatro oros en dificultad y dos en combinada), es el primero en repetir un mismo 9c y en pionero al aunar en sus manos dos vías de la máxima dificultad cuando alguien confirme 'B.I.G.'. Antes de completar 'DNA' ya había intentado las otras vías 9c salvó 'Café Colombia'.

images.caption: Jakob Schubert, en la vía 'DNA'.

articles.title: F1 Announces African Grand Prix in Rwanda, Posts Photo of Proposed Circuit for Race in 'Early 2030s'
articles.summary: Formula One announced Tuesday a 10-year agreement to bring the African Grand Prix to Rwanda starting in the "early 2030s."
articles.body:
Formula One announced Tuesday a 10-year agreement to bring the African Grand Prix to Rwanda starting in the "early 2030s."

An F1 race has not been held in Africa since 1993 when the South African Grand Prix took place for the final time at the Kyalami Grand Prix Circuit.

In addition to Tuesday's announcement, F1 showed a rendering of the circuit planned to be built just south of Rwanda's capital city of Kigali:

Aside from Africa and Antarctica, F1 currently stages races on every other continent, so reintroducing Africa into the fold cements the league's global status.

F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali released a statement on the agreement with Rwanda, saying, "Today is a landmark moment for Formula One. With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade, our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the World Championship closer than ever to fans around the globe. Africa has always been part of Formula One's future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way, with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating meaningful impact."

The exact starting date of the new African Grand Prix in Rwanda isn't yet clear, but the final two South African Grand Prix races were held in the month of March in 1992 and 1993.

Legendary French driver Alain Prost, who won four career F1 points titles, was the final winner of the South African Grand Prix, beating out Ayrton Senna in 1993.

articles.title: Australia bowl out South Africa to win first cricket Test in Durban
articles.summary: Hazlewood’s 6-49 ⁠⁠helped the visitors clean up the South African batting, securing the win before tea on day five.
articles.body:
Australia’s pace bowler Josh Hazlewood has bowled his side to a 214-run ⁠⁠victory over South Africa on the last ⁠⁠day of the first cricket Test match at the Kingsmead Stadium in Durban.

The hosts’ resistance ended before tea on Tuesday as they were dismissed for 206.

Hazlewood took 6-49 ⁠⁠as Australia bagged the six wickets they needed on the last day to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

He struck twice in one over with the new ball after ⁠⁠already having taken two wickets on Monday and then breaking through South Africa’s stoic early fightback.

The 35-year-old Hazlewood also removed the last batsman to ensure the victory in the first clash between the teams since South Africa upset Australia in last year’s World Test Championship final at ‌‌Lord’s in London.

South Africa held out for the first 110 minutes of Tuesday’s play before a legside delivery from Hazlewood was edged by Wiaan Mulder and snagged by a diving catch from wicketkeeper Alex Carey.

Mulder and Aiden Markram resumed at 102-4 overnight, and the pair extended the fifth-wicket partnership to a patient 69 runs off 205 balls before Hazlewood’s breakthrough, with Mulder making 29.

Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw, who was the man of the match ⁠⁠for Australia with the bat, then took a second Test wicket ⁠⁠when Kyle Verreynne quickly followed Mulder back to the change room with a reckless shot that saw him caught at slip by Steve Smith without scoring.

South Africa were 166-6 at lunch and added 25 runs before the new ⁠⁠ball was taken, but crumbled quickly thereafter.

Marco Jansen was bowled by Hazlewood for 35 and three balls later Simon Harmer followed as he brushed ⁠⁠the ball through to Carey with his glove.

Markram then ⁠⁠fell after a patient 75 off 237 balls, edging Mitch Starc’s delivery off his pads to be caught behind, but was only given out after a television review.

Hazlewood then completed the win as tailender Anrich Nortje popped up the ball ‌‌to short midwicket for Nathan Lyon to catch.

Former Australia captain Smith, who did not field in Monday’s late session after a blow to the head while batting, returned to action on ‌‌Tuesday.

“Steve ‌‌Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning,” a statement said.

Travis Head celebrates after the dismissal of South Africa’s Anrich Nortje sealed victory for Australia [Marco Longari/AFP]

articles.title: Rwanda to host a Grand Prix in 2030s as Formula One returns to Africa
articles.summary: Rwanda has secured a 10-year deal to host F1 races at a purpose-built race track on the outskirts of the capital, Kigali.
articles.body:
Kigali, Rwanda – Formula One will return to Africa after a decades-long absence, with Rwanda scheduled to host a Grand Prix in the early 2030s.

Rwandan President Paul Kagame made the announcement during a ceremony attended by Formula One President and CEO Stefano Domenicali and FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem in Kigali on Tuesday.

“Rwanda has been working very hard towards hosting the African Grand Prix,” Kagame said. He referred to it a “partnership” that was long overdue but “a milestone for the continent”.

The East African nation has secured a 10-year deal to bring Formula One back to the continent for the first time since 1993, with the inaugural race projected for the early 2030s.

The Grand Prix will be held near Kigali, with former Austrian motorsport driver Alex Wurz’s racetrack design firm in charge of designing the new circuit.

It will be built near the Bugesera international airport, 40 kilometres (24.8 miles) south of Kigali.

The circuit will stretch over six kilometres, with 17 corners and an anti-clockwise layout. Designed to follow the natural terrain, it will feature an elevation gain of 197 metres per lap. The track will be developed to FIA Grade 1 standards and is expected to host other motorsport competitions and major events.

Kagame emphasised that “Rwanda is happy and excited to be part of a journey that will change how Africa is conceived by the world of sports”.

Mohammed Ben Sulayem, president of the sport’s governing body, hailed Formula One’s return to Africa as “a moment of immense pride”, adding that it opened “a new chapter in the history of Formula One”.

Formula One chief Domenicali termed Africa “the missing piece” in the championship’s global footprint.

In December 2024, the Rwandan president announced the country’s bid to host a Formula One Grand Prix during an address to the FIA General Assembly in Kigali.

Lewis Hamilton, Formula One’s most successful driver with seven world titles and 106 Grand Prix wins, has been a leading proponent of the competition’s return to Africa.

At last week’s Singapore Grand Prix, Hamilton was asked about the prospects of an F1 race in Africa and reiterated his stance, saying: “We need to have a Grand Prix in Africa.”

“It is, for me, the most important continent, to be honest, the most beautiful continent,” the Ferrari driver said. “We’re on all the other continents but that one and there should be no reason for it.”

The British driver is known to have advocated for an F1 race in Africa for years and has publicly urged F1’s Domenicali to add a race in Africa.

“It is something I’ve been pushing for in the background, and Stefano has been amazing,” Hamilton said last week.

“He’s flown to Africa so many times over the last couple of years, speaking to lots and lots of different people, so I hope that he has some news for me soon.”

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, the reigning world champion, also expressed his excitement.

“We want to race in a lot of different places in the world, so I really hope that it can be pushed through,” he said.

“I’ve been once to Rwanda. We have to wait to see if it’s all going to go through, but I think we’re all very excited if that happens.”

Rwandan President Paul Kagame [Laith Mushtaq/Al Jazeera]
Qatar’s Ambassador to Rwanda, Mansour Ali Fahad Al-Shahwani Al-Hajri, left, attended the ceremony announcing the return of Formula One to Africa [Laith Mushtaq/Al Jazeera]
Lewis Hamilton has urged F1’s leadership to add a race in Africa [File: Jakub Porzycki/Reuters]

Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

The 32-year-old journeyman has played his usual brand of chaotic football since taking over as the Giants starter, but the production has led to consecutive top-12 fantasy finishes.

The Saints' uptempo style should lead to another solid stat line for Winston in Week 6. Just know, he's more of a one-week streamer than a rest-of-season solution in your lineup.

Cousins is coming off his first down game in a blowout loss to the Patriots, but he's still a top-10 fantasy quarterback on the season after throwing for multiple touchdowns in his first four appearances.

You can expect the veteran to rebound in Week 6 against a Bills defense that's been a plus-matchup for fantasy QBs and will be playing on a short week. Buffalo-Las Vegas is also tied for the highest projected point total early in the week at 52.5.

Though it's only a matter of time before Fernando Mendoza takes over, Cousins will be a solid fantasy streamer until that happens.
