Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is sidelined, Tank Bigsby (core) is on injured reserve and now Will Shipley (plantar fascia) is expected to miss multiple weeks. That's on top of the injuries to Philly's offensive line and receiving corps.

Enter Pierce, who is the literal definition of next man up. It's easy to forget, but Pierce was once the Texans starter during his rookie season back in 2022. During that campaign, he posted 1,104 scrimmage yards, 30 receptions and five touchdowns. Since then he's mostly bounced around the league as a depth piece and practice squad player.

While we'll have to monitor Barkley's health to see if he has a chance to suit up in Week 6, at the moment it seems like Pierce will get the start.

Fortunately for him, the matchup with Jacksonville can help explain away his embarrassing efficiency on Sunday with just 14 rushing yards on 11 carries, as well as negative two yards on two receptions. His next opponent, the Panthers, have allowed at least 75 scrimmage yards to every starting RB they have faced in the opening month. If Pierce gets the call, he'll be a low-end RB2 for fantasy.

The Chargers backfield is the definition of a hot-hand committee with Vidal, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell splitting snaps almost evenly the last two weeks.

Vidal gets the mention here coming off his best game of the season, thanks to 57 yards and a touchdown on eight carries. He's also increased his snaps each week since the opener (7%, 10%, 25%, 35%, 42%).

You shouldn't expect any of the Chargers backs to run away with the lead job, but each are usable in fantasy as RB3 options.

The Browns backfield is a mess, so much so that I had to give them a writeup in this section. Quinshon Judkins left the stadium in a walking boot on his right foot, which is the side his season-ending ankle injury occurred on last year. It's possible it's just precautionary, but it puts his Week 6 status in doubt until we get an update.

Dylan Sampson is on IR with a knee injury that was initially expected to keep him out until later in the season, but head coach Todd Monken said there's a chance the team could open his practice window this week. We'll keep an eye on that, but I'd expect Sampson to still be a few weeks away from returning.

With Sampson sidelined, Sanders has been the No. 2 back in Cleveland. However, Sanders also came out of this game with a hip injury that we'll need to get more information on. If Judkins is out and Sanders is healthy enough to start, he would be in the high-end fantasy RB3 mix.

If Judkins and Sanders can't suit up, then we're looking at a tandem of Jaleel McLaughlin and Jaret Patterson (practice squad). In that scenario, McLaughlin would be a dart-throw flex at best against Baltimore.

Given the current state of the waiver wire options, I want to make sure managers are considering some of the sneakier options available in a lot of leagues.

If Coleman was dropped, you should be stashing him in your IR spot. J.K. Dobbins found the end zone in Week 5, but he hasn't played well this season. RJ Harvey has also failed to make a case for the lead-back role.

Meanwhile, Coleman flashed with 58 yards, three catches and a touchdown the last time he was on the field. The rookie is a no-risk investment that could pay off in a big way in the second half of the season.

This is an extreme long shot, but Conner is a potential trade candidate who's sitting on IR in Arizona. I have the veteran stashed in several leagues, just in case the Cardinals send him to an RB-needy roster before the deadline.

Woody Marks is 54% rostered but would be the No. 1 RB add, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Chris Rodriguez Jr. vs. HOU (35% rostered)

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

Bernard is a nice combination of an intriguing rookie, a new opportunity and some proof of concept already with his six-catch, 80-yard effort on nine targets in Week 5.

That was aided by injuries to Michael Pittman Jr. being on IR and Roman Wilson leaving the game with a finger issue that's expected to keep him out multiple weeks.

In the meantime, Bernard ran a season-high 94% of the routes on Sunday. He's also earned praise from Aaron Rodgers , who can be mercurial with his pass-catchers.

Until Pittman or Wilson are back, Bernard can be started as a fantasy WR3 with upside.

Even before the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, you could have made the argument that Bourne was the more valuable fantasy asset. Now that MHJ is headed to the Texans , Bourne is solidified in his role behind the top two pass-catchers, Trey McBride and Michael Wilson.

Jalen Brooks saw the biggest change in his role with Harrison out of the way, but Bourne was by far the more productive option — catching five of his eight targets for 70 yards against the Lions. That's the second time this season Bourne has reached those totals.

Some harder matchups are on the way, but moving forward, Bourne can be started as a fantasy WR4/flex option.

Jordyn Tyson is 49% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add and can be stashed in your IR spot, if available.

Malik Washington is 49% rostered but would be the No. 3 WR add behind Tyson and Bernard, if available.

Wan'Dale Robinson is 52% rostered but would be the No. 5 WR add behind Tyson, Bernard, Washington and Bourne, if available.

Khalil Shakir is 50% rostered but would be the No. 6 WR add behind Tyson, Bernard, Washington, Bourne and Robinson, if available.

Jakobi Meyers is 50% rostered but would be the No. 7 WR add behind Tyson, Bernard, Washington, Bourne, Robinson and Skakir, if available.

Strange is making a case to be in the low-end TE1 conversation, following a pair of quality outings with at least eight targets both times. That resulted in back to back top-12 fantasy finishes thanks to stat lines of 7-95-0 and 7-68-0.

While many non-elite tight ends have fantasy success due to touchdown-scoring, Strange is earning the kind of volume that could make his production more sustainable. Given his role in one of the best offenses in the league, Strange needs to be rostered.

Speaking of tight ends who are boosting their fantasy numbers with TDs, Freiermuth found the end zone twice on Sunday to bring his season total to four.

His seven targets are also notable, making it the fourth time in five outings he's had at least five passes thrown his way.

Even with Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson sidelined, it's hard to project a significant yardage total for Freiermuth, but his steady role combined with the TD upside makes him a fantasy starter through the bye-week gauntlet.

Hunter Henry is 52% rostered but would be the No. 2 TE add behind Strange, if available.

Dart-throw streaming options (if starter is out)

Patriots are 51% rostered but would be the No. 2 D/ST add behind the Chiefs, if available.

Ravens are 59% rostered but would be the No. 3 D/ST add behind the Chiefs and Patriots, if available.

Quarterbacks: Bo Nix, Justin Herbert, Sam Darnold

Running Backs: David Montgomery, Jadarian Price, Jonathon Brooks

Wide Receivers: Chris Godwin Jr., Brian Thomas Jr., Michael Pittman Jr.

Tight Ends: Jake Ferguson, Dalton Schultz

Bo Nix has been held under 15 fantasy points in four of his five games this season and now has to face the Seahawks defense in Week 6.

Meanwhile, Justin Herbert can only dream of putting up 15 fantasy points. He's failed to accomplish that feat in all five outings this year.

David Montgomery left Sunday's game with a groin injury that could sideline him for multiple weeks. Even prior to leaving that game, the veteran back had been struggling to generate production. Since his three-touchdown game in Week 1, Montgomery has averaged just 32 scrimmage yards per game (never topping 50 yards) and hasn't scored another TD.

At this point, the only hope for Brian Thomas Jr.'s fantasy outlook would come through a trade, but the Jaguars remain adamant that they aren't interested in dealing him away. Over his last three games, BTJ had managed stat lines of 1-8-0, 2-17-1 and 0-0-0 while playing limited snaps.

articles.title: Week 6 Fantasy Waiver Wire: Woody Marks, Dameon Pierce, Brenton Strange, Germie Bernard and MORE
articles.summary: Week Six of the NFL season is set to begin, starting with a Thursday night matchup as the Seattle Seahawks take on the Denver Broncos in a Super Bowl XLVIII...
articles.body:
Week Six of the NFL season is set to begin, starting with a Thursday night matchup as the Seattle Seahawks take on the Denver Broncos in a Super Bowl XLVIII rematch.

It's unfortunate that this has become normal, but injuries throughout the league have once again hindered fantasy rosters, and bye weeks are now officially underway, with the Bengals, Dolphins, Lions and Vikings off this week.

Good news: there are a number of players who can step in, be of use to your roster and make a lasting impact. Below is my full waiver wire column, going over the players, by position, that managers should target this week.

I know some of these players may not be available in every league, so I solely look for players rostered in less than 60 percent of leagues.

Jordan Love – Green Bay Packers (Rostered: 47.9%): Love has improved his game over the past two games, averaging an impressive 9.2 yards per attempt and completing 77 percent of his throws with four touchdowns. A big part of his improvement is that his receivers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, have both played exceptionally. Love is a great streaming option for the next couple of weeks, with the Cowboys and Lions on deck.

Aaron Rodgers – Pittsburgh Steelers (Rostered: 19.3%): Over his last three games, Rodgers has scored 28.68, 27.96 and 28.0 fantasy points. The 42-year-old continues to exceed expectations, averaging 275.3 passing yards per game and throwing for three touchdowns in all three contests. Despite the Steelers' wide receiver room becoming thin, head coach Mike McCarthy has found ways to use other players, like Pat Freiermuth and Germie Bernard. While he's still hot, Rodgers should be rostered and streamed.

Jameis Winston – New York Giants (Rostered: 4%): The Winston experience is like no other in the league. At times his up-and-down play is hard to trust, but the way he's connected with Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers over the last two weeks, throwing three touchdowns in each game, has bolstered my confidence in the 32-year-old. If your QB is on a bye this week, Winston is definitely worth adding.

Zach Charbonnet – Seattle Seahawks (Rostered: 57.5%): Charbonnet is very close to being removed from my list (rostered in less than 60 percent of ESPN leagues) as he inches closer to a return. This likely isn't the week he comes back, but it's wise to jump ahead now if he's available. Charbonnet will immediately be the featured back in a good Seattle offense and will have plenty of chances to find the end zone. His floor in fantasy is viewed as a low-end RB2, with an RB1 ceiling thanks to his touchdown-scoring ability.

Woody Marks – Houston Texans (Rostered: 48%): Expect Marks to take control of the Texans' backfield with David Montgomery nursing a groin injury. Last week, Marks rushed for 62 yards on 15 carries and caught all four of his targets for 23 yards. Even before the injury, Montgomery was losing red-zone snaps to Marks and has been underwhelming since his monster game in Week One. The severity of Montgomery's injury is still to be determined, but even without it, Marks has earned the starting role.

Dameon Pierce – Philadelphia Eagles (Rostered: 2.4%): Pierce is the next man up in the Eagles' depleted backfield. Saquon Barkley is listed as week-to-week, Tank Bigsby landed on injured reserve, and Week Five starter Will Shipley has a plantar fascia tear, which should sideline him for a handful of games. I wouldn't prioritize Pierce, but if you're in need of a running back, he's likely the most available option for Week Six.

Kendrick Bourne – Arizona Cardinals (Rostered: 1.7%): With the Cardinals having traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans over the weekend, Bourne is now the team's WR2 behind Michael Wilson. He caught five of eight targets for 70 yards in Week Five against the Lions. It's hard to expect much from Bourne with Trey McBride and Wilson demanding a lot of the targets, but he immediately has an increased role on one of the league's most pass-heavy teams, which is usually chasing points in most games.

Germie Bernard – Pittsburgh Steelers (Rostered: 3%): Bernard has so far developed into the receiver the Steelers have been needing in their offense. The second-round rookie ran the same number of routes as DK Metcalf (28), led the team with nine targets and posted six catches for 80 yards. With Michael Pittman Jr. on injured reserve and Roman Wilson expected to be out a couple of weeks, Bernard is in line for more opportunities and has breakout potential if Aaron Rodgers continues his recent sharp play.

Keenan Allen – Indianapolis Colts (Rostered: 37%): Allen is someone who won't blow you away, but he's someone you'd want in a PPR league. Over his last two games, he's seen nine targets in each and caught at least five passes for 45 yards or more. His involvement in the Colts' offense should stay the same while Alec Pierce is on injured reserve, which is enough reason to roster the veteran wideout.

Ryan Flournoy – Dallas Cowboys (Rostered: 4.3%): Flournoy is the fantasy beneficiary when either CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens is unavailable. Lamb missed some snaps last week, which allowed Flournoy to post a season-high 90 yards on three receptions. In five games this season, Flournoy has seen at least four targets in each. Lamb is currently dealing with a quad bruise, but it isn't considered serious. Whether Lamb suits up or not this week, Flournoy should be picked up as a valuable handcuff stash in a very potent offense.

Brenton Strange – Jacksonville Jaguars (Rostered: 27.2%): Over the last two weeks, Strange has put up a team-high 26.2 percent target share and leads the team in targets (16), receptions (14) and yards (163). Despite the Jaguars' crowded receiving room, he has shown himself to be Trevor Lawrence's security blanket alongside Parker Washington. Strange has a tough matchup against the Texans this week, but he should still be streamed until something changes.

Pat Freiermuth – Pittsburgh Steelers (Rostered: 20.3%): Freiermuth finished last week against the Colts with a pair of touchdowns, catching five of seven targets for 44 yards. It's the second week in a row he's found the end zone and posted at least five targets. With the lack of options at receiver for the Steelers, expect the Penn State product to continue to see more usage in a matchup against the Buccaneers, who've allowed the 10th-most fantasy points to tight ends.

Darren Waller – Carolina Panthers (Rostered: 20.7%): Waller is a very touchdown-dependent tight end in fantasy. However, before the Panthers' bye, he caught eight of 14 targets for 87 yards over his last two games, showing he's getting more involved and building chemistry with Bryce Young. There are most likely better and safer options at the position, but his recent increase in usage and his touchdown upside make him one of the better available choices.

Kansas City Chiefs Defense (Rostered: 33.5%): The Chiefs' defense is a better real-life defense than a fantasy one. However, Kansas City is coming off its bye to take on the Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium. Los Angeles' offense has been terrible all season, recording an NFL-most 13 turnovers and getting sacked at the second-highest rate (10.6 percent) in the league. The Chiefs' defense is a premier streaming option for Week Six.

San Francisco 49ers Defense (Rostered: 36.3%): Last week, the Niners' defense intercepted Seattle's Sam Darnold twice and sacked him five times in the team's 32-29 win in Seattle. San Francisco has posted 11 sacks this season and will have a date with the Commanders at home in Week Six. Last week against the Giants, Washington's Jayden Daniels was sacked five times. The Niners' defense is another top-tier streaming option.

articles.title: Rangers CHL, USHL prospects notebook: Andre Mondoux career-best output
articles.summary: It was another productive week for New York Rangers prospects across the CHL and USHL, highlighted by a breakout offensive […]
articles.body:
It was another productive week for New York Rangers prospects across the CHL and USHL, highlighted by a breakout offensive performance from Kingston defenseman Andre Mondoux .

Several prospects continued strong starts to their seasons, while others battled through mixed results as league play intensifying here in October.

Rangers Prospect of The Week – Andre Mondoux (Kingston Frontenacs)

Last Thursday night featured an OHL matchup between Rangers defenseman prospects, when Mondoux and the Kingston Frontenacs skated to a 7-4 win over Evan Passmore and the Barrie Colts.

Mondoux turned in the best offensive performance of his OHL career, recording two goals and one assist for a career-high three-point night. His efforts earned him second-star honors

Mondoux scored twice in the second period, including the game-tying goal at 11:57. The 19-year-old followed that up by picking up a secondary assist on the go-ahead — eventual game-winning — goal by Alex Misiak 5:44 into the third period.

Mondoux can RIP IT 🚀 André Mondoux scores twice for the Frontenacs in the 2nd period🤯 pic.twitter.com/AhFU9Wjm2J — Kingston Frontenacs (@KingstonFronts) October 9, 2026

Mondoux can RIP IT 🚀 André Mondoux scores twice for the Frontenacs in the 2nd period🤯 pic.twitter.com/AhFU9Wjm2J

Kingston Frontenacs (@KingstonFronts) October 9, 2026

The following night, Mondoux scored his third goal in two games, when the Frontenacs defeated the Brampton Steelheads 4-2. With Kingston trailing 1-0 in the first period, Mondoux blasted a shot home after stepping in from the left point to tie the game.

André Mondoux can't stop scoring😤🚨 pic.twitter.com/VIyEhuYML5 — Kingston Frontenacs (@KingstonFronts) October 9, 2026

André Mondoux can't stop scoring😤🚨 pic.twitter.com/VIyEhuYML5

Mondoux extended his point streak to three games with an assist Saturday against the Brantford Bulldogs in a 4-2 victory.

As impressive as the offensive production was, Mondoux likely should use his heavy shot more consistently. He recorded five shots against Barrie but managed only one against Brampton and didn't record one against Brantford.

Mondoux is tied for third on Kingston with four goals, and has seven points in 10 games.

Rest of Rangers Prospects in CHL and USHL

It was another frustrating week for Passmore as Barrie lost each of its three games.

On Thursday against Mondoux and Kingston, Passmore was held scoreless despite recording five shots on goal. He finished the game with a minus-one rating.

Saturday saw Niagara hand Barrie a 4-2 defeat. Passmore, Barrie's captain, again didn't record a point.

On Sunday, Barrie traveled to Erie to face the Otters. Though the Colts lost 3-2, Passmore provided one of the bright spots, scoring his second goal of the season. With Barrie trailing 2-0 in the second period, Passmore joined an odd-man rush and beat the Erie goaltender at 7:09 to pull his team within one at 2-1.

Passmore has two goals, 16 penalty minutes and is minus-6 in nine games this season.

Wednesday against the Kitchener Rangers, Darian Anderson picked up a primary assist when he slipped a pass between two Rangers defenders to find Cooper Williams alone in front for a goal. Williams walked in and snapped a shot over the shoulder of Kitchener's goalie to give Flint a 3-1 lead, in what ended up to be a 5-2 victory.

The assist extended Anderson's season-opening point streak to six games.

Saturday, the 19-year-old forward added two more assists to his ledger. Just one minute into the game, Anderson earned a secondary assist when he moved the puck to Jimmy Lombardi, who found Williams for a one-timer that beat Sarnia goaltender Ivan Tkach-Tkachenko and gave the Firebirds an early 1-0 lead.

🚨Cooper Williams 🍏Darian Anderson 🍏Jimmy Lombardi pic.twitter.com/Bu00ORo5zM — Flint Firebirds (@FlintFirebirds) October 8, 2026

🚨Cooper Williams 🍏Darian Anderson 🍏Jimmy Lombardi pic.twitter.com/Bu00ORo5zM

Flint Firebirds (@FlintFirebirds) October 8, 2026

Later, with Flint clinging to a 5-4 lead, killing a penalty, and under a minute remaining in regulation, Anderson set up Lombardi for the empty-net short-handed insurance goal at 19:45 to seal the 6-4 victory.

The leading scorer among Rangers prospects, Anderson has a seven-game point streak, leads Flint with five goals, and is second with 10 points.

Spencer Bowes began his week by scoring Ottawa's lone goal in a 2-1 overtime loss to Niagara on Thursday. His goal came at 7:01 of the third period and tied the game. It also extended his season-opening ppint streak to six games.

The 2026 fourth-round draft pick was held off the score-sheet Saturday against Erie for the first time this season, but still contributed in Ottawa's 3-0 shutout victory. The forward finished with three shots on goal, a plus-one rating, and won six of his 11 face-offs.

On Sunday, Bowes picked up his sixth goal of the season, when the 67's needed a shootout to defeat Brantford 4-3. With Ottawa trailing 1-0 in the first period, Bowes got his team back on even terms when he fired a shot from a sharp angle that appeared to bounce off the end boards, then off the Bulldogs goaltender and into the net.

12 🤝 13 @NYRangers prospect Spencer Bowes scores his 6th goal of the season off a nice setup from @Avalanche prospect Ondrej Ruml. #NYR | #GoAvsGo | @OHLHockey pic.twitter.com/n6Qh9SjHfc — Ottawa 67's (@Ottawa67sHockey) October 11, 2026

12 🤝 13 @NYRangers prospect Spencer Bowes scores his 6th goal of the season off a nice setup from @Avalanche prospect Ondrej Ruml. #NYR | #GoAvsGo | @OHLHockey pic.twitter.com/n6Qh9SjHfc

Ottawa 67's (@Ottawa67sHockey) October 11, 2026

Bowes ends the week as the leading goal scorer among Rangers prospects with six. He's tied for eighth in the OHL goal-scoring race and also has eight points in eight games.

Zeb Lindgren recorded his third assist of the season 35 seconds into the third period of Red Deer's 8-5 victory over the Calgary Hitmen on Friday. While the final score appeared close, Red Deer controlled much of the game and at one point held a commanding 7-3 lead.

On Canadian Thanksgiving on Monday, Lindgren was held off the score-sheet but was credited with one shot on goal when Red Deer earned a 4-0 victory over the Edmonton Oil Kings, their fourth consecutive win.

The 19-year-old defenseman has three assists and is plus-6 in nine game games for the Rebels, who sit atop the Central Division in the WHL with a 6-2-0-1 record.

Defenseman Artem Gonchar was scoreless and recorded two shots on goal while also taking a hooking minor Thursday, when the Sudbury suffered their first loss of the season, falling 4-3 in overtime to North Bay.

Friday saw the Wolves fall behind the Peterborough Petes 3-1 before launching a comeback. It was Gonchar who got Sudbury going, setting up Rowan Hendrickson for a power-play goal at 7:14 of the second period.

It was Gonchar's only point of the game, but it helped spark six unanswered goals by the Wolves, and Sudbury rallied for a 7-3 victory. The win improved the Wolves to 6-0-1 on the season. They are the only OHL team without a regulation loss , and are currently first in the Central Division.

Friday was a difficult outing for goaltender Danai Shaiikov , who was pulled at the 6:38 mark of the second period with the Olympiques trailing the Baie-Comeau Drakkar 3-1. He allowed three goals on nine shots and appeared uncomfortable throughout the game.

Fortunately for Shaiikov and the team, backup goaltender Finn Moffett stopped all 11 shots he faced. Gatineau rallied to erase the deficit, and forced overtime before ultimately winning 4-3 in a shootout. The comeback spared Shaiikov from being charged with the loss.

Sunday brought more struggles when Shaiikov surrendered five goals on 22 shots in a 6-3 loss to the Val-d'Or Foreurs.

The difficult weekend took a toll on his statistics. Skaiikov fell to 3-1-2, while his goals-against average rose to 3.23 and his save percentage dropped to an unsightly .868.

On Monday, Shaiikov served as the backup goaltender, when the Olympiques lost 3-2 to the Chicoutimi Saguenéens.

On Friday, Felix Farhammar saw his five-game point streak come to an end, when the Muskegon Lumberjacks fell 5-0 to the Chicago Steel in USHL action. Farhammar was credited with two shots on goal and finished the game with a minus-2 rating.

Saturday saw Farhammar bounce back with a secondary assist on Muskegon's second goal in a 5-4 loss to Chicago. New York's 2025 seventh-round pick was not credited with a shot on goal and finished the contest with a minus-1 rating.

Farhammar continues to make a strong impression in the early stages of his USHL career. He's third on Muskegon with six points (two goals, four assists) in eight games.

articles.title: 2026-27 Fantasy Basketball Draft Strategy: Hacking the default rankings
articles.summary: Using multiple data points in draft prep can help fantasy managers unearth value picks.
articles.body:
For those who take fantasy basketball seriously, a big part of preparation is checking (and comparing) rankings from multiple sites. Identifying outliers can help managers find value regardless of draft format, from consistent late-round contributors to players with league-winning potential.

In this article, we'll compare our preseason rankings with ESPN, Yahoo! and Fantrax, focusing on players whose predicted values vary by significant margins.

Your one-stop-shop for all of Rotoworld's preseason content leading into fantasy basketball drafts.

Based on the rankings, we rank Anunoby higher than the other sites. Despite his scoring average dropping by more than a point per game from 2024-25, the Knicks forward provided third-round value in 12-team leagues. During the Knicks' run to the title, Anunoby averaged 20.1 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.6 assists, 1.5 steals, 1.1 blocks and 2.6 three-pointers per game.

Can he produce similar numbers during the regular season, especially if the Knicks stick with the offensive approach that won them the title? That is certainly conceivable. Also, Anunoby's availability wasn't an issue in either of his first two full seasons in New York, as he played 74 and 67 games.

Twenty-three seasons in, LeBron continues to hold off "Father Time." Fantasy managers can no longer justify drafting the future Hall of Fame forward in the first two rounds, but James should still offer top-50 value, at a minimum, in his new home. During the offseason, there were discussions about James taking on some point guard duties to lighten Tyrese Maxey 's workload.

However, with the 76ers already lacking depth at center and losing Ariel Hukporti to an Achilles tendon rupture, James will likely be asked to play small-ball center at times. He can certainly make plays for himself and for others in that role, and matching up with bigger foes could raise LeBron's fantasy ceiling. ESPN's ranking is the outlier, with him just inside the top 75.

Banchero can be a tricky player to pinpoint in fantasy basketball. While percentages have weighed down his value in the past, the overall production can't be ignored. Based on his past production, Yahoo and Fantrax rate the Magic forward highly heading into the 2026-27 season. The question is how new head coach Sean Sweeney will impact the Magic roster, a talented young group that still has offensive strides to make.

After 78 games in Philadelphia over two seasons, the team traded George to Boston in exchange for Jaylen Brown . He'll take on a key role with the Celtics, and an offensive system that isn't hesitant to shoot three-pointers could benefit him. The question is: how much should fantasy managers factor in his recent availability issues?

The ESPN and Yahoo rankings seem to hold the injuries against George, while ours and Fantrax's rankings appear to be more forgiving. If George stays on the court, he has good odds of exceeding preseason expectations, regardless of which rankings you prefer.

Morant has long been a tricky player to value in fantasy basketball properly. Even with the turnover concerns, the Trail Blazers guard can be an electrifying option when he's on his game. However, availability matters, too. After appearing in at least 61 regular-season games in three of his first four seasons, Morant has played 79 over the last three. Unfortunately, fantasy managers have to plan for at least one injury-related extended absence, and there have also been suspensions in the past.

In Portland, he joins a backcourt with plenty of options, including Damian Lillard , Jrue Holiday , and Scoot Henderson . And then there's Deni Avdija , who took on playmaking responsibilities for most of last season and enjoyed his best year as a pro. While our rankings and Fantrax give Morant a more optimistic outlook heading into the 2026-27 season, Yahoo and ESPN are more skeptical.

How much room for growth does a player have who offers little to no scoring value but is one of the NBA's best defenders? That's what we'll find out with Thompson, who averaged 9.9 points per game last season. He averaged 26.0 minutes per game, and preseason talk in Detroit is that Thompson will play more minutes. If so, that raises his fantasy ceiling, even with the lack of scoring.

Ausar averaged 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists, 2.0 steals and 0.9 blocks per game last season, numbers that helped salvage most of his value in category leagues. Based on the rankings, ESPN and Fantrax view him more favorably going into the 2026-27 season than we do, largely because of his limited scoring output.

It's a new era in Memphis, and while most of the conversation has focused on lottery pick Cameron Boozer , Coward should also be a factor. However, Yahoo values the second-year wing much more than any other outlet used for the column. The question is whether Coward can offer more value in the defensive categories than he did as a rookie. He averaged 0.6 steals and 0.4 blocks per game as a rookie, numbers that didn't make much of a mark when assessing his fantasy value.

Coward has room to grow offensively, and he should have every opportunity to step up now that players like Ja Morant and Jaren Jackson Jr. are no longer in the picture. Whether he exceeds overall fantasy expectations may depend on his defensive contribution, especially steals.

While Queen had some good moments as a rookie, he still had a long way to go defensively. Although the Pelicans were already out of contention for a postseason spot, his playing time dropped by about five minutes per game in March, mainly because of his defense. Queen finished the season on a decent run, averaging a double-double in six April appearances, which may have shaped how some fantasy experts view him.

ESPN, Fantrax and Yahoo all have Queen as a top-100 player in their rankings, but we aren't so sure. Yves Missi , who brings more defensively, has started at center in the preseason. Queen can still be a valuable option for fantasy managers, but expecting a top 100 return may be a bit much, especially if new Pelicans head coach Jamahl Mosley sticks with Missi (who appears to be a better fit next to Zion Williamson ) as his starting center.

articles.title: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones reacts to fan yelling ’embarrassing’ at Dak Prescott
articles.summary: Jerry Jones defends fans’ right to criticize the Cowboys.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has defended a fan who yelled "embarrassing" at quarterback Dak Prescott after the team's disappointing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Jones said he had no problem with the confrontation involving the NFL fan following Dallas' 24-16 defeat at AT&T Stadium last Thursday.

"It doesn't impact me at all," Jones said. "The driver in question was not an employee. Fans can express themselves, and should express themselves."

The incident went viral after Prescott encountered the man while walking through the stadium tunnel. The individual was initially believed to be a stadium employee but was later identified as a transportation driver working for a third-party car service.

Speaking of which, Jones said, "Whether he was our employee or not, he was a fan, it sounds like. So, I'm for our fans expressing themselves."

During the incident, Prescott had turned toward the man after hearing the remark and challenged him to repeat it. He also gestured toward security during the exchange.

Jerry Jones backs fan criticism amid Cowboys' struggles

Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) looks to throw the ball during the game between the Cowboys and the Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The confrontation followed another frustrating performance for Dallas, which fell to 2-3 after losing to a Buccaneers team that entered the game winless.

Prescott later explained that the criticism itself was not the main issue. He objected to the man appearing to retreat after making the remark.

"Feel free to speak your mind — just speak it," Prescott said. "If you're saying it to me, then say it to me. Don't go back on it."

The driver subsequently claimed in a TikTok video that he had been fired. He accepted responsibility for the comment but questioned why Prescott had not shown similar emotion during the game.

Jones' response reflects his view that paying fans have the right to express frustration. However, the incident also highlights the pressure surrounding Prescott as Dallas struggles to find consistency. The Cowboys quarterback has produced strong individual numbers this season, but the team's results remain disappointing.

Jones has also acknowledged his frustration with the team's performance, saying, " I'm obviously disappointed in our results so far." So, Dallas must address its defensive problems and improve its execution if it hopes to change the direction of their season.

articles.title: Grading Patriots QB Drake Maye's dominant performance against Raiders
articles.summary: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye played one of the best games of his career in Week 5 against the Raiders.
articles.body:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye played sensationally in the team's 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5.

Maye deserves an "A+" for his performance in the win over the Raiders. He put together one of the best games of his young career and helped New England improve to 3-2 on the season after falling into a 1-2 hole to begin the year.

The 24-year-old Maye completed 26-of-34 passes for 374 yards and four touchdowns, adding seven carries for 25 yards and a rushing touchdown. His 76.5 percent completion rate and 150.9 passer rating were both season highs, and he posted a quarterback rating of 96. Maye spread the ball effectively, with DeMario Douglas catching two touchdown passes and Hunter Henry and Kyle Williams each adding one.

Most importantly, Maye did not throw an interception for the first time this season. He entered the game with seven interceptions through four weeks, including three in the season opener against the Seattle Seahawks and two in Week 3 against the Jacksonville Jaguars. His clean performance against Las Vegas marked a major step forward in terms of him taking care of the ball, and it gave the Patriots ' offense the boost it needed to produce a huge scoring output in the game.

Maye's five total touchdowns and 399 yards of offense powered a season-high of 536 total yards for New England, which has now won consecutive games heading into Week 6.

articles.title: Ivica Zubac spent the summer trying to make himself a perfect fit in the Pacers fast-paced offense
articles.summary: INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Ivica Zubac got a brief glimpse into the Indiana Pacers track-like offense last season.Then he went back to Europe, worked on his conditi...
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Ivica Zubac got a brief glimpse into the Indiana Pacers track-like offense last season.

Then he went back to Europe, worked on his conditioning and returned to the U.S. early to figure out how he fit with his newest teammates.

No, the 7-foot, 240-pound Zubac doesn't really look like a natural in this rapid, high-scoring style, but he's doing everything he can to make a successful transition from traditional center to one who can keep up with speedy All-Star Tyrese Haliburton and the rest of the Pacers.

"Once I rebound or inbound the ball, he (Haliburton)'s already looking ahead, throwing the ball ahead," Zubac said. "I'm more used to point guards who spend more time with the ball, who hold the ball longer than him. He's getting off of it quick and it's the team in general. The system is based on making quick decisions and guys making quick reads."

He spent his first 9 1/2 NBA seasons playing in Los Angeles — for either the Lakers or Clippers — and emerged as a defensive stalwart who was willing to mix it up around the rim while setting hard screens.

That's not how the Pacers have been playing since overhauling their roster following the acquisition of Haliburton near the trade deadline in 2022. Indiana's moves have been mostly to add quick, athletic players at each position so they can operate at full throttle. Even longtime center Myles Turner could run the court effectively.

But when Turner made the surprise decision to sign with the rival Milwaukee Bucks instead of returning to the Eastern Conference champs in July 2025, the Pacers were left with a glaring hole already knowing Haliburton would miss the entire season because of a torn right Achilles tendon. An early rash of injuries sealed Indiana's fate in a lost season.

So when the Pacers saw Zubac available at the trade deadline, they jumped — sending the Clippers two players and multiple draft picks, including a 2026 first-round selection that turned out to be an unprotected lottery pick. It was a costly move, but one they don't regret.

"I think as you look at last season into this offseason, I felt like and I think as a staff we felt that our team was right there — we're right on the cusp of being a championship team," general manager Chad Buchanan said. "So why should we be patient and wait for something else down the road? Why should we be thinking long term? Like it's right there in front of us and we felt like an opportunity to get a top 10 center in our league at that position was a big need for us. This is a player that fits what our roster needs right now."

The Pacers believe Zubac will keep up with the pace and also will help improve facets that were weaknesses previously — setting screens to create open looks for 3-point shooters or on drives to the basket, rebounding and defense.

Zubac was a second-team All-NBA defensive selection in 2024-25. He was not eligible for the team last season because injuries limited him to just 48 games, including only five with the Pacers.

Still, it was enough to show Zubac what he needed to work on over the summer and, so far, Haliburton likes the early results.

"It's a different dynamic than playing with Myles in the sense of Myles is obviously more of a finesse player, a space shooter," Haliburton said. "Zu is a guy who's really a very physical guy, hard screen-setter, roller, plays more above the rim with lobs and rebounding. It looks a little different, but honestly when I came into the league, I thought that was the archetype I needed to play with to be successful."

Zubac has been through weeks of workouts now that started with what's become a regular trip to Nashville and morphed into full-court workouts before training camp opened.

How long it will take to get on the same page is unknown. What's not is coach Rick Carlisle's ability to adjust his plan to who he has available.

"Rick is a brilliant coach, and our coaching staff has shown the ability to adapt to different types of players and they'll figure out how to maximize some of the things maybe that he does that's different from how we have played," Buchanan said. "There's a lot of things Zu does bring to this group that I think will accentuate what we already have in-house."

And Zubac is eager to show he'll give the Pacers exactly what they need to be a championship contender, too.

"I don't think it's going to take long," Zubac said when asked about the chemistry between him and Haliburton. "We didn't spend much time together on the court (before camp), but the time we did it felt really natural for me. It was never hard playing with smart point guards. We don't need much time to gel together. Like I said it's natural."

Staal suffered a tear in his calf during warmups before Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Flyers. The 38-year-old forward was subsequently ruled out of the contest, and the Hurricanes announced that he would miss "significant time" as he recovers from the injury.

Although the team has not provided a specific timeline for his return, Staal could potentially be sidelined for a couple of months, leaving Carolina without one of its most important leaders during a crucial stretch of the season.

Staal enjoyed a memorable campaign last season, earning the Conn Smythe Trophy as the most valuable player of the Stanley Cup playoffs while captaining Carolina to its first Stanley Cup championship in 20 years.

The veteran forward previously won a Stanley Cup with the Pittsburgh Penguins in 2009, giving him experience winning championships with two different franchises.

His absence will challenge the team's depth and leadership, particularly as the Hurricanes attempt to build on last season's championship success.

Carolina hosts the Washington Capitals on Tuesday, providing its first opportunity to demonstrate how it will respond to the loss of its captain.

With Staal expected to miss significant time, the Hurricanes will need contributions from across the roster to maintain their momentum while their veteran leader focuses on recovering from his injury.

articles.title: Dodgers Should Copy Brewers' Fix For A Slumping Star Instead Of Benching Shohei Ohtani
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are reportedly going to discuss benching Shohei Ohtani
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are going to have a conversation with Shohei Ohtani about potentially benching him, according to The Athletic's Fabian Ardaya.

Ohtani has been playing through injuries, and his struggles at the plate are becoming a bigger issue. The Dodgers are down 0-2 to the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series, and they cannot afford any more terrible offensive performances. However, benching a player who could go down as the greatest of all time might not be the solution.

Ohtani is not the only problem right now for the Dodgers, but he is one of them. He is also one of the players who could instantly turn this series around. He can be part of the fix, and the Dodgers should take a page out of the Milwaukee Brewers' playbook to help their offense without benching their best player.

Christian Yelich had a solid start to the season, and then hit a wall. On Aug. 3, he was hitting .234 with a .687 OPS. He had hit in the top four spots of the lineup in every game to that point, but the Brewers knew something had to give. They did not bench him or platoon him. They dropped him down in the order. It took some pressure off Yelich, and it brought some better bats to the top of the lineup. Yelich's numbers did not really improve, but the offense as a whole was better, and he looked more comfortable.

He was not the only Brewers' star to get bumped down. William Contreras was also dropped down in the order for a while, but earned his way back up by getting hot. Yelich also earned his way back up into the two-hole in the postseason against the San Diego Padres by getting hot.

In fact, in the postseason, Yelich and Contreras have been the two best hitters on the team. Manager Pat Murphy knew that benching his stars was not a fix. However, the Dodgers are deeper than the Brewers, so they may view things differently.

Benching Ohtani for Josue De Paula could be a move the Dodgers make, but it seems hard to believe that the Dodgers offense will fix itself without Ohtani as part of the solution.

articles.title: Bourdais, Moss headline second batch of Sebring's 75 all-time greatest drivers
articles.summary: Fifteen more iconic racers join the 'Class of 75' celebration ahead of the milestone 75th Mobil 1 Twelve Hours of Sebring
articles.body:
Four-time Indy car champion Sébastien Bourdais and British motorsport icon Sir Stirling Moss headline the second group of inductees selected to the "Class of 75," an elite list honoring the most successful drivers in the history of the Mobil 1 Twelve Hours of Sebring. The complete roster of 75 drivers is being revealed in five batches of 15 between September and January, leading up to the historic 75th running of the endurance classic on March 20, 2027.

The hall-of-fame style roster was compiled and voted on by a 10-person panel of sports car racing experts to commemorate the landmark anniversary. Sebring International Raceway held its inaugural 12-hour race on March 15, 1952, and the event has run continuously ever since – with only a single cancellation in 1974 due to the global energy crisis.

The selected drivers have been divided into randomly drawn groups of 15. Following the initial reveal on September 15, the second set of 15 drivers named to the "Class of 75" features a diverse mix of international sports car legends:

Always-fast Italian driver Michele Alboreto capped his Sebring career with an overall victory in 2001, driving the No. 1 Audi R8 for Team Joest alongside Rinaldo Capello and Laurent Aiello in a rare caution-free race—a feat achieved only three times in track history (1985, 1994, 2001). In his 1995 debut, Alboreto set the fastest qualifying time in the Team Scandia Ferrari 333SP before finishing fourth. He followed it with a runner-up finish in 1996 and three consecutive runs with Team Joest in an Audi R8 (1999–2001), progressing from third to second before taking the overall crown.

Though a native of Le Mans, France, Bourdais makes his home just over 100 miles from Sebring in St. Petersburg, Florida, and has ruled the Central Florida circuit like his own backyard. With three wins, 11 podium finishes, and 985 laps led, Bourdais is exceptionally comfortable at the track. After debuting in 2001, he broke through for a GT3 class win in 2006 driving a Panoz Esperante GTLM for Multimatic. He later secured overall victories in 2015 (Action Express Corvette DP) and 2021 (JDC-Miller Motorsports Mustang Sampling Cadillac alongside fellow Frenchmen Tristan Vautier and Loic Duval).

#5 Mustang Sampling / JDC-Miller MotorSports Cadillac DPi, DPi: Tristan Vautier, Loic Duval, Sebastien Bourdais

Capello holds the second-most overall victories in the history of the Mobil 1 Twelve Hours of Sebring. His five overall wins across just nine starts are an extraordinary achievement, especially given that his worst career finish at the track is fourth (one second, two thirds, and three fourths). Capello's Sebring career spanned from a third-place finish with Team Joest in an Audi R8 in 1999 to his final run in an Audi R18 in 2012, where he stood on the top step alongside Tom Kristensen and Allan McNish.

One of the rare drivers on the "Class of 75" roster who competed in the inaugural 12 Hours of Sebring in 1952, Briggs Cunningham logged 14 starts and secured three class victories (1953, 1962, and 1964). Better known as a legendary car owner, Cunningham's entries captured three consecutive overall wins from 1953 to 1955. Over his career, he drove and fielded a diverse array of machinery, including Ferrari, Jaguar, Corvette, Maserati, Porsche, and his own Cunningham C4R and C6R.

In 10 starts at Sebring between 1956 and 1970, German driver Hans Herrmann experienced feast or famine. In half of those races, he finished first overall or on the class podium; in the other five, he failed to finish. Making his debut in 1956, he drove a factory Porsche 550 Spyder to a class win and sixth overall. He captured his first overall 12-hour victory in 1960 driving a Porsche RS60 with Olivier Gendebien, winning by nine laps, and took a second overall crown in 1968 with Jo Siffert in a factory Porsche 907. He also earned class wins in 1966 and 1967.

Always behind the wheel of a Porsche and nearly always running at the front of the field, Al Holbert was a Sebring fixture. His first overall victory came in 1976 in a Porsche Carrera RSR alongside Michael Keyser, winning by two laps. His second overall triumph followed in 1981 in a Porsche 935 with Hurley Haywood and Bruce Leven. Holbert added podiums in 1983, 1985, 1986, and 1987, immortalizing the legendary Lowenbrau livery on his Porsche 962 in the minds of sports car fans worldwide.

Frenchman Nicolas Lapierre made every one of his three Sebring appearances count, winning twice and finishing fourth on the lead lap in his only other outing. His debut in 2011 yielded a victory alongside Loic Duval and Olivier Panis in a Peugeot 908 HDI FAP, and he returned to the top step seven years later in 2018 in a Nissan DPi for Tequila Patron ESM with Pipo Derani and Johannes van Overbeek . His other appearance came in 2016, driving a Nissan to fourth overall.

#22 Tequila Patron ESM Nissan DPi, P: Nicolas Lapierre

Jyrki Juhani Järvilehto -- universally known as JJ Lehto -- boasts one of the most remarkable winning percentages in Sebring history. Across just seven starts, the Finnish driver visited victory lane six times: twice as an overall winner, twice as an overall runner-up, once third overall, and once third in class. His first overall victory came in his 1999 debut in a BMW V12 LMR alongside Tom Kristensen and Jorg Mueller, after also claiming pole position. He secured his second overall win in his final Sebring start in 2005, sharing an Audi R8 with Kristensen and Marco Werner.

Jan Magnussen put together an ironclad streak of 21 consecutive starts at Sebring from 1999 to 2019, visiting victory lane nine times—all behind the wheel of a Corvette. The Danish ace captured five GT class victories: first in 2006 with Oliver Gavin and Olivier Beretta , followed by wins in 2008, 2009, 2015, and 2017 alongside Antonio Garcia , Ron Fellows, Johnny O'Connell, and Mike Rockenfeller . He also added class runner-up finishes in 2007 and 2012, and third-place results in 2005 and 2019.

When the world's top automotive manufacturers arrived at Sebring in 1954, international superstars followed, including British icon Stirling Moss. Moss scored a famous upset victory that year driving an underpowered OSCA entered by Cunningham and shared with Bill Lloyd. Though he made only nine starts at Sebring, his 1954 overall win was complemented by a sixth-place finish in 1955 and a class victory with a second-place overall finish in 1956 aboard a Maserati.

Though initially set on a different path, John Paul Jr. was pushed into racing by his father after high school and quickly proved his championship mettle. In only his second Sebring start in 1982, father and son teamed up to drive their family-owned Porsche 935 to an overall victory after leading the final 100 laps. Paul Jr. followed up by setting the fastest qualifying time in 1983, later finishing second overall in 1993 with Gianpiero Moretti and Derek Bell in a Nissan GTP-ZXT, along with three additional top-five finishes before closing his career in 2000.

Brian Redman's 1975 victory marked a major milestone: BMW's first U.S. victory at the 12 Hours of Sebring, which also served as Redman's first overall win in the Florida endurance classic, shared with Allan Moffat, Sam Posey, and Hans Stuck. He followed it up with a second Sebring overall win in 1976 aboard a Porsche 935 with Charles Mendez and Bob Garretson. Redman's illustrious record also includes overall podiums in 1979 (Porsche 935) and 1987 (Porsche 962), as well as a third-place class finish in 1991 in a Mazda RX-7 with a four-rotor engine.

Swiss star Jo Siffert's six starts at Sebring were highlighted by an overall victory in 1968 alongside Hans Herrmann in a factory Porsche 907. A factory effort the previous year yielded a second in class and fourth overall, also with Herrmann. Siffert starred in the iconic Gulf Porsches before his career was tragically cut short, collecting a third-place finish in 1966, a class runner-up finish in 1970, and a class third in his final Sebring appearance in 1971.

#54 Porsche 907LH: Vic Elford, Jochen Neerpasch, Jo Siffert, Rolf Stommelen, Hans Herrmann

Modern fans know Wayne Taylor as a powerhouse team owner, but he spent years as an elite championship driver, making 11 starts at Sebring. His pinnacle driver success came in 1996 with Doyle Racing, taking overall victory in a Riley & Scott Oldsmobile Mk III alongside Eric Van de Poele and Jim Pace . The South African native also took class runner-up finishes in 1994 and 1998, and sixth overall in 1999 and 2000. As a team owner, Wayne Taylor Racing has added two overall Sebring victories to his resume in 2017 and 2024.

A world-class racing driver who also competed at an elite level in skiing as a younger member of the French National Ski Team, Bob Wollek was a formidable presence at Sebring. Though he captured only one overall victory -- dominating the field by four laps in 1985 aboard the Swap Shop Porsche 962 with A.J. Foyt -- Wollek was perpetually a threat. He secured class second in 1998, and third overall in 1984 (with Foyt) and 1991. Tragically, Wollek lost his life on the eve of the 2001 race when he was struck by a van while riding a bicycle near the track.

The reveal of this second group of 15 legends continues the countdown to the historic 75th-anniversary milestone. The third installment of 15 drivers will be announced on November 10, 2026, followed by the fourth group on December 15, and the final 15 on January 12, 2027, completing the full "Class of 75" roster.

articles.title: Devils’ loss to Ottawa exposes a familiar problem: ‘We’ve got to learn how to score when it’s hard’
articles.summary: The Devils failed to earn their offense in a loss against the Senators.
articles.body:
The Devils knew what was coming. They still couldn't find a way through it.

Hours before Monday's game at Prudential Center, coach Sheldon Keefe described Ottawa as one of the NHL's best checking teams. The Senators would take away space, make it difficult to move through the neutral zone and force New Jersey to work for its offense.

The Devils lost 4–1, falling to 2–3 after another game spent chasing a lead. Arseny Gritsyuk's first goal of the season spoiled the shutout late, but it did little to change the takeaway: When an opponent shuts down their rush game, the Devils still struggle to manufacture offense another way.

"We've got to learn how to score when it's hard," Keefe said afterward. "That's just the reality of it."

It's only five games. There is plenty of time to work through new combinations and get players comfortable. But the concern is less about the record than the familiar way this loss unfolded.

Ottawa protected the middle, allowed New Jersey to possess the puck on the perimeter and made the Devils fight for anything close to Senators goalie Linus Ullmark.

"They give you the outside, and then you can play there all night," Devils winger Jesper Bratt said. "You can circle in the O-zone as much as you can. But if you don't get to the inside, it's not really any good ice."

The Devils finished with a 30–20 advantage in shots. That didn't mean they consistently made Ullmark's night difficult.

"We made tonight a little too easy on Ullmark," Bratt said. "He's a good goalie when he sees the puck."

That was a significant difference from Saturday's win over Vancouver, when New Jersey's power play scored three times. Against Ottawa, the Devils went 0-for-2 and couldn't generate enough at even strength.

Keefe wants more from the line of Jack Hughes, Bratt and Anthony Mantha. That responsibility extends beyond Mantha trying to find chemistry with two established teammates.

"We'd like more, but I'd like more from Jack and Bratt, too," Keefe said. "Those guys have to find their way inside more. Chances on the rush, if they're not available, we've got to find different ways to score."

Bratt said the line is still building familiarity. He also acknowledged that playing alongside him and Hughes comes with an adjustment.

"We're instinct players, and we're fast," Bratt said. "Sometimes we're maybe in areas where we shouldn't be, and then we're transitioning fast."

Asked whether embracing the approach was a buy-in issue, Keefe described the challenge as both mentality and instinct.

"Jack and Bratt don't play an interior game, and they're some of the biggest drivers of our team," he said. "We've got to find different ways for them to get to the inside consistently so they can be dangerous that way."

The Devils also made the night harder on themselves with penalties.

They escaped the first period scoreless despite a five-minute boarding major to Mantha and minors to Brenden Dillon and Luke Hughes.

But Ottawa forward Shane Pinto scored nine seconds into the second period at even strength.

"Right from the drop of the puck, our brains weren't switched on to start the period," Keefe said. "To start like that, with some of our most experienced people on the ice, is unacceptable."

Ottawa added a power-play goal later in the period. New Jersey had allowed the first goal for the fifth straight game and was back in a position that is becoming far too familiar.

"It's not fun chasing the game, going down goals over and over," Devils defenseman Brett Pesce said. "We've got to find a way to get the first one."

Pesce also offered a straightforward assessment of the Senators that he thinks the Devils could emulate.

"They play a simple game," he said. "They get it in. They wear our D out. They stay on the hunt. We could take a little page from their book, to be honest."

articles.title: Georgia flips CB Nash Johnson from Auburn: ‘I feel like Georgia can prepare me for the next level’
articles.summary: Georgia has flipped another talented in-state prospect from an SEC rival. Powder Springs (Ga.) McEachern cornerback Nash Johnson has switched his commitment...
articles.body:
Georgia has flipped another talented in-state prospect from an SEC rival. Powder Springs (Ga.) McEachern cornerback Nash Johnson has flipped his commitment from Auburn to Georgia, giving Kirby Smart and the Bulldogs another important addition to their secondary.

Johnson's recruitment has taken several turns. He initially committed to Alabama before reopening his recruitment and eventually choosing Auburn. But Georgia continued building its relationship with the talented defensive back, and the Bulldogs gradually gained momentum.

Johnson visited Athens in September, and his conversations with Georgia's staff became increasingly significant as the season progressed. The decision to flip didn't happen overnight.

"I've been thinking about this decision for a while now, especially throughout the summer when I stayed in communication with the coaches," Johnson told Rivals.

Georgia's track record of developing defensive backs played a major role in Johnson's decision. So did the opportunity to grow under Smart and his staff.

"I like what they have going on, the way they develop DBs, and how I feel like they can help me grow not just as a football player but as a man too. I feel like Georgia can prepare me for the next level and push me to be the best version of myself on and off the field."

Georgia's pursuit gained traction while Johnson remained committed to Auburn. The Bulldogs stayed in contact, continued making their pitch and ultimately convinced him that Athens offered the best opportunity for his future.

Johnson also wanted to make clear that his decision wasn't driven by outside circumstances.

"It's not about money or the situation with anybody else, it's about what I feel is best for my future," Johnson said. "I've prayed on it and really thought about it, and Georgia is somewhere I can see myself growing and succeeding."

Smart's approach to coaching was another major factor.

"Coach Smart holds his players accountable and pushes them to be great at everything they do," Johnson said. "It's bigger than just football with him, he wants his players to be disciplined, tough, and carry themselves the right way as men.

"I feel like being around a coach like that would push me out my comfort zone and help me grow on and off the field."

For Georgia, the flip represents another recruiting victory within its home state and against an SEC competitor.

articles.title: “I Would Have Just Slapped Mike”: Jarvis Landry Doesn’t Believe Mike Evans’ Explanation After “Disrespectful” Roast of Trevon Diggs
articles.summary: One of the most iconic moments of the NFL season took place on Sunday as the San Francisco 49ers came up against the Seattle Seahawks. Mike Evans of the 49er...
articles.body:
One of the most iconic moments of the NFL season took place on Sunday as the San Francisco 49ers came up against the Seattle Seahawks. Mike Evans of the 49ers appeared to troll his adversary, Trevon Diggs, by checking his name on the back of the shirt as the duo argued about something, leading to a reaction from the entire football world.

While many laughed it off, Jarvis Landry seemed to take exception to the behavior shown on the field by Mike Evans. The former Miami Dolphins wide receiver made it clear he would have "slapped" Mike Evans if he tried something similar on him.

"My instincts, I would have just slapped Mike for like just as soon as he would did I just slapped him like my that alone check try to check my nameplate like to check my nameplate bro that's disrespectful bro," Landry said.

"You get the chart of numbers and the names on during the week when you do the scout study. So you know who it is already out there."

Evans Explained His Actions After The Game

When asked about the incident after the game, Mike Evans appeared to suggest he genuinely had no clue who the player under the helmet was.

"I mean, I was blocking him until the whistle, and then [Diggs] said something like I'm doing extra or something like that," Evans said to the media, as reported by NBC .

"And I didn't know that was him at first, because I played against him a few times and we always been cool, you know, he's a good player. I honestly didn't know it was him because in the helmet, it's hard to tell sometimes, and you know, we were just talking trash.

"I think I like pushed him, and then I was like, 'Who are you?' And I looked to make sure … And then he mushed me. It should have been a penalty. But yeah, I mean, it is what it is."

The 49ers are back in action against the Commanders on Monday with Mike Evans set to start.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream management failed players and fans with WNBA Finals arena conflict
articles.summary: Why didn't the Dream have a contingency plan for where to play these games?
articles.body:
The WNBA Finals are scheduled to begin in four days, and as of now, the Atlanta Dream don't have a desirable home venue for the series. I'll need someone to explain to me how that's possible.

From here, it looks like straight-up negligence and management malpractice.

What we're being told is that State Farm Arena, the 17,044-capacity home of the Hawks and where the Dream played their previous playoff games, is already booked on the dates Atlanta is scheduled to host the Golden State Valkyries . And the Dream's regular home, Gateway Center Arena, is too small to host the finals, with its capacity of 3,500, but remains the fallback plan as efforts to find a larger venue have failed, according to USA TODAY Sports .

What that doesn't explain is why the team waited until now to find a contingency plan. I'm no expert in the field of venue booking, but isn't this something they could have ironed out before the season started? Or at least before the playoffs. Unless Dream management thought there was no way the team would still be alive right now. In which case, way to believe!

That doesn't completely check out either, though. The Dream were a playoff team and No. 3 seed last year, trending up after trading for Angel Reese. They were expected to be good. They also knew they were outgrowing Gateway Center because they sold out every game there the last three years, according to a release from the team announcing State Farm Arena as their new home beginning in 2027. Oh, and they sold out State Farm eight times in that span too.

All signs were pointing to a team with a passionate fanbase that would predictably show up if the Dream made a deep playoff run. And because they don't share ownership with the Hawks or State Farm Arena, they needed to have a backup plan for how to accommodate those fans.

With better planning, the Dream might've been able to gain priority at State Farm over the Sombr concert scheduled Oct. 22, the same day as Game 3, but they were never going to bump the Hawks games on Oct. 24 and 29, which overlap with Games 4 & 6 of the WNBA Finals. There's certainly some bad luck involved with the scheduling, but the Dream needed to have another arena lined up for this worst-case scenario come true.

The WNBA was incentivized to make sure they had a plan too. According to Sports Business Journal , teams contribute 20 percent of their net finals gate up to $500,000 to the league.

Instead, all parties apparently sat on their hands, and Atlanta's players and fans will pay the price -- literally. If the game is played at Gateway Center, the few fans fortunate enough to attend will pay a premium to get in. The players won't get the full big-arena experience they deserve for the biggest games of their lives. And if the Dream find an alternate venue last minute, it'll be a new environment for everyone. Which isn't ideal either.

This was a failure on the Dream's part. The players and fans deserved better.

Week 5 was not a banner week for NFL head coaches. And it continued into Monday night as the Los Angeles Rams fell to the Buffalo Bills in overtime.

Though Rams coach Sean McVay laid some of the blame at the feet of his kicker , he also took accountability for his role in setting up the missed field goal that set up Buffalo to win the game:

"I wish I would've had a better play call and gone for, gotten it a lot tighter. I'm sick right now with myself," McVay said. "And I'm so proud of that group. This is the tough part of sports, but I'm proud of that team. I'm proud of the way that we battled and I'm sick that we came up short. I'll be regretting kicking that and not having a better call to be able to go for it on third down. It's on me."

At least the coaches are all owning up to their mistakes .

articles.title: SA vs AUS: Steve Smith cleared of concussion after helmet blow, returns to field in Durban Test
articles.summary: Steve Smith was struck by a delivery during Australia's second innings and subsequently passed concussion tests. After not fielding during South Africa’s inn...
articles.body:
Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead in Durban on Tuesday, after undergoing a series of clinical assessments following a blow to the helmet. The 37-year-old batter was struck by a short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje during Australia's second innings. Smith attempted to duck under the ball but misjudged its trajectory as it failed to rise as much as he expected. Although he continued batting after the incident, scoring 27 off 41 balls before being caught at long-on off Simon Harmer, Smith did not take the field when South Africa began their second innings on Monday. Michael Neser served as his substitute fielder during that session. However, Smith returned to the field on Tuesday morning after being cleared under Cricket Australia's concussion protocols. He was stationed in the slip cordon when South Africa resumed their chase and subsequently took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling. "Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia's concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," Cricket Australia said in a statement.

Smith's concussion history raises concern after helmet blow

The incident brought back memories of Smith's previous concussion scare during the 2019 Ashes in England, when he was struck on the head by fast bowler Jofra Archer and forced to miss part of a Test match. Smith's return to the field came after medical assessments over the preceding 24 hours, with Australia following the prescribed protocols before allowing the experienced batter to resume his duties. His presence was a boost for Australia as they pushed for victory in the series opener, with South Africa mounting a determined resistance on the final day.

Australia close in on victory as South Africa lose two wickets

South Africa resumed at 102/4 on Tuesday, needing another 319 runs to win. They reached 166/6 by lunch after Australia struck twice to strengthen their grip on the contest. Opener Aiden Markram led the home side's resistance, remaining unbeaten on 69 at the interval alongside Marco Jansen on seven. The pair had to rebuild after Wiaan Mulder's patient 69-run fifth-wicket partnership with Markram ended when Josh Hazlewood had Mulder caught behind by Alex Carey. Part-time spinner Matt Renshaw then dismissed Verreynne, who made just one before edging a reckless shot to Smith at slip. Renshaw has been Australia's standout performer with the bat, having scored 190 in the first innings and 82 in the second, before adding two wickets to his match contribution. Australia needed four more wickets at lunch to seal victory in the opening Test. The second Test of the series is scheduled to begin in Gqeberha on Sunday.

articles.title: Kyle Whittingham Defends Zack Marshall After Leaked Texts
articles.summary: Kyle Whittingham defended tight end Zack Marshall, calling the leaked group-chat texts a lapse in judgment. #GoBlue
articles.body:
Michigan Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham met with reporters Monday and made clear that quarterback Bryce Underwood and offensive coordinator Jason Beck are both staying put coming out of the bye week. He also addressed the story that hung over the program for the past week: tight end Zack Marshall criticized the coaching staff in a group chat, and screenshots of those text messages were released online.

Marshall apologized on X on Tuesday, Oct. 6, after the Wolverines' loss to Minnesota. "This game is won and lost as a team, and I pointed fingers instead of taking accountability," he wrote . It was the biggest story about the Michigan football program during the bye week.

Kyle Whittingham Defends Zack Marshall At Monday Press Conference

Whittingham did not distance the program from Marshall. "Zack Marshall's a great young man. He's a team guy. It was just a lapse in judgment or an error in judgment. And he apologized profusely to myself and the team," Whittingham said , per Wolverines Wire.

He was not willing to write the whole thing off, either. "Yeah, people get frustrated. Yeah, you get frustrated. You lose a couple games. People get frustrated," Whittingham said. "It doesn't matter if it was in a small group chat. It was in a small, close circle. That's beside the point. The point is you've got to protect the team. And it wasn't protecting the team."

The leaked messages called Beck a problem, and a week later he is still the one calling the Michigan offense . "Jason is calling plays and Bryce is our guy," Whittingham said of the two decisions fans wanted an answer on. The Wolverines sit at 3-2 after back-to-back losses to Iowa and Minnesota, and the only personnel change Whittingham announced was a new punt returner.

Zack Marshall Still Has No Catches This Season

Marshall has not recorded a single catch this season for Michigan. The tight ends have not been used much in the Wolverines offense this season. If the Wolverines offense does not change for the better against the Penn State Nittany Lions on Saturday, then maybe Marshall's comments were justified.

articles.title: World Artistic Gymnastics Championships: Russian trio denied visas by Netherlands
articles.summary: The Netherlands deny visas to three Russian gymnasts leaving them unable to compete at next week's World Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam.
articles.body:
The Netherlands has denied visas to three Russian gymnasts leaving them unable to compete at next week's World Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam, Russia's governing body says.

Reigning women's all-around world title holder Angelina Melnikova is among the trio, which also includes Viktoria Listunova and Anna Kalmykova.

The Russian Gymnastics Federation (RGF) has labelled the decision "discrimination" and a "violation" of the principles of equal competition, accusing the Dutch authorities of deliberately trying to keep the "strongest gymnasts" out of the event.

"The Embassy of the Netherlands in Moscow has notified the visa centre of its refusal to issue visas to three leaders of the Russian women's national team," the RGF said in a statement.

"As a result, the gymnasts have been deprived of the opportunity to compete at the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships."

Russia said it would appeal against the decision to the World Gymnastics governing body and the International Olympic Committee (IOC), with the competition due to run from 17-25 October.

In August, Melnikova was initially denied a visa to compete at the European Championships in Croatia.

The decision was reversed on appeal and she subsequently won the all-around gold medal.

The move from Dutch officials means the world championships will be affected by visa refusals for a second consecutive year.

Israeli gymnasts, including defending world floor champion Artem Dolgopyat, were denied entry to Indonesia for the 2025 championships in Jakarta because of the country's involvement in the conflict in Gaza.

Russia is scaling up its push to be brought back into the world of sport, following years of restrictions after its invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and the uncovering of state-sponsored doping at the 2014 Winter Olympics in Sochi.

In July the IOC eased restrictions on Russian athletes , opening a path for them to compete in qualifying events for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

articles.title: LSU men's, women's basketball won't attend SEC Tip-Off due to weather
articles.summary: Neither of LSU's men's and women's basketball teams will attend SEC Tip-Off in person due to weather, the school has announced.
articles.body:
LSU men's and women's basketball will appear remotely for SEC Tip-Off on Tuesday, Oct. 13, due to weather, the school announced .

The SEC Tip-Off is the conference's official preseason media event in Birmingham, Alabama, where coaches and players talk with reporters to kick off the season. While the other 15 teams will appear in person at the Grand Bohemian Hotel, LSU coaches Kim Mulkey and Will Wade won't attend.

Fog is the culprit for LSU's travel issues, both teams said. There are no storms or rain in the forecast for either Baton Rouge, Louisiana, or Birmingham, Alabama, for Oct. 13.

Wade was previously scheduled to meet with media at 10:35 a.m. ET, whereas Mulkey was to talk at 11:35 a.m. ET. Wade was slated to bring guard Abdi Bashir Jr. and forward Mo Dioubate, with Mulkey bringing Mikaylah Williams, MiLaysia Fulwiley and ZaKiyah Johnson.

There are plenty of storylines around LSU men's basketball and Wade, who's in his first season with the program of his second tenure after previously being fired by the program after the 2022 season due to recruiting violations.

The LSU roster has 10 players officially listed on it as the team is working around numerous eligibility situations , including former Big East Player of the Year RJ Luis, who previously signed NBA contracts with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics.

Mulkey, meanwhile, has also had quite the offseason. Returning Ukrainian center Kate Koval left the team after LSU signed Russian transfer Anna Minaeva. Koval, whose dad serves in the Ukraine military, was uncomfortable sharing a team with a Russian player amid the two countries' conflict after Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

LSU women's basketball was picked to finish third in the conference, whereas the men's team was picked 14th amid its roster uncertainty.

articles.title: “We’ve Lost Sight of That”: LSU Legend Raises Concerns on Lane Kiffin’s “$40 Million Roster” Management After Upset Loss vs. Kentucky
articles.summary: Lane Kiffin spent more than $40 million on NIL to assemble his roster for his debut campaign with the LSU Tigers. However, the team’s playoff hopes are in sh...
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin spent more than $40 million on NIL to assemble his roster for his debut campaign with the LSU Tigers. However, the team's playoff hopes are in shambles after Saturday's disappointing 35-34 overtime loss to the Kentucky Wildcats.

On Monday's episode of the " 4th and South " podcast, former LSU stars Jarvis Landry and Leonard Fournette discussed Kiffin and his team after the loss to Kentucky. Landry compared the current team to their time with the program and raised concerns about LSU's future despite the multimillion-dollar NIL investment.

"They're really good at defense," Landry said. "They fly around. They get hands to the ball. Whatever it is. But when I played during my time there, during your time there, what I saw was man-to-man press coverage. We don't care who y'all are. We are better. We don't need no help. We not bracketing nobody. And I feel like this new age defense, they are bracketing. "They are playing more cover three-quarters, all of this cover two. Bro, it's man on man, big on big, we better than y'all. And I feel like we've lost sight of that at LSU. The same way we lost sight of a fourth-and-one game on the line. We have a $40 million roster. We can't get one yard with $40 million?"

The same way we lost sight of a fourth-and-one game on the line. We have a $40 million roster. We can't get one yard with $40 million?"

Landry played for LSU from 2011 to 2013 as a wide receiver. During his college career with the program, he recorded 1,809 yards on 137 receptions and 15 TDs before being drafted No. 63 by the Dolphins in 2014.

The LSU Tigers had a 27-24 lead in the fourth quarter. However, Adam Zouagui's field goal forced the game into overtime. Quarterback Sam Leavitt's 15-yard rushing TD put the Tigers ahead 34-27.

However, the defense failed to keep Kentucky at bay. Running back CJ Baxter scored a one-yard rushing TD to make it 34-33. The Wildcats then sealed the win with a successful two-point conversion attempt.

Lane Kiffin Blames Lack of Execution as Reason for Loss to Kentucky

In the postgame press conference, Lane Kiffin said that the reason LSU lost to Kentucky was that they failed to execute the chances they had.

"If you don't execute, then you don't execute," Kiffin said. "The punt return, got a player there tackling him and doesn't tackle him, you know, and it goes outside. The long run, we get scooped out of the gap and the ball goes for a long run. So, if you don't do fundamentally sound stuff, you get exposed versus good teams."

The LSU Tigers (4-2) will next face Mississippi State (4-1) on Saturday, Oct. 17.
